review_title: Alfred Brendel - live joyfulness and romantic mood in Schubert sonatas
review_text:
Schubert was central to Alfred Brendel's repertoire since the early days of his longish and prestigious performing career. Year by year, the legendary Austrian pianist seemed to deepen his insights when it came to Schubert and refine his means by fresh inspiration to approach this wonderful musical realm. A well-balanced touch and deeply heart-felt way of playing entered the stage in Brendel's Schubert recordings and his live performances. The latter unfolded in addition - due to their unitary conception and realization - a rich world of feelings and ideas conjured up on spot, much inspired in their mood and carefully chiseled on their sound side.
This twofer gathers four live recordings of Brendel comprising Schubert sonatas, achieved between 1997 and 1999 in Amsterdam, Frankfurt, London and Aldeburgh. If A major (D 959), B flat major (D 960) and G major D 894) sonatas are here nothing but some valuable repeats, the B major one (D 575) is a new entry in his recorded repertory.
All in all, this release is a welcome pretext to celebrate and enjoy Brendel's masterful craftsmanship in his dearest musical realm.

review_title: I use this every single day
review_text:
I'm a Mac person but Microsoft really got me with Office 365. At first I was annoyed to have a subscription service but since I'm part of a family of 5, it worked out that we got our money's worth. Office isn't a perfect application--I LOVE Excel more than Numbers and Word is more complete than Pages but can t clunkier, not organized as well, and not as good for Desktop publishing and images. But Office at this price is excellent.
The next thing I hated was that 365 switched from the number of devices to the number of users. I could STAND that my home computer that my 3 kids used had to have separate logins for applications on the same computer. BUT, when Dropbox continually refused to offer smaller monthly packages and limited the number of devices on their free version, I started to look elsewhere. Lo and behold Microsoft OneDrive was my answer. And it was ALREADY INCLUDED with my Office 365. Now everyone in my family has 1 TB of OneDrive storage and they can access it on their iphones, laptops or wherever they can get an internet connection. I can share REALLY LARGE VIDEO FILES with as many parents from the school that I want. I can share lots of school videos for the parents to download AND I don't have to store them on my computer. In other words I can have them on the cloud (OneDrive) and they don't have to sync to my computer. This frees up a lot of space on my computer. (I save copies on external drives of course.) Good-bye Dropbox!
So this has become an essential part of my life and one of the subscription services I consider a must-have along with Amazon Prime.

review_title: Good for that tough one on your gift list...

We all know that the best thing that you can give someone is a personalized gift to show that you care. But there are times that you also know that some individuals would appreciate an Amazon gift card, if simply because they're saving up for something very special, and a few of these allow them to reach that goal.

This [[ASIN:B00ADR3HS2 Amazon.com Gift Card - In a Gift Box]] turned out to be perfect for the individual for whom it was picked, and for last minute gifting, the free one-day shipping helps. Just be aware that there's a barcode on the back that tells the recipient "To redeem, visit amazon.com/redeemgift" so it could take away from the surprise if the person is somewhat inquisitive.

I've used these Amazon Gift Cards quite a bit over the years in a number of the variations, by email, print at home, as mail in a greeting card and even as a post to Facebook. They can vary by style and denomination, so just pick the one that's most appropriate for the recipient and go for it.

The [[ASIN:B00ADR3HS2 Amazon.com Gift Cards - In a Gift Box]] is a good one as a primary for that tough one on your gift list, or as a supplementary gift, and from personal experience, both as one who has given them and as a recipient, they are highly appreciated.

review_title: The tax return service... that didn’t file taxes.
review_text:
Turbotax is a lot like McAfee virus protection; they advertise everywhere, but they’re a rotten company through and through.

Everythings seems easy and friendly, until something actually goes wrong. I tried filing my taxes through turbotax last year—at the cost you see here—only to find out months later they filed nothing. Nada. Did they email me? Call? Contact or warn me in any way? Nope. I followed every step, paid in full, and they did... nothing.

You had ONE job, turbotax.

So then I made the mistake of trying to call them. For help, right? Good luck with that. Only if you pay for the highest possible service can you speak to a human being. Otherwise, it’s an automated run-around directing you to useless pre-recorded messages and urging to visit their website. I did find help online.... from other users who had also gotten screwed over by turbotax.

Save your money. I wish I had been warned. Don’t assume popularity means quality. Like anything else, it just means they advertise more.

Recently, I was clearing my parents house out and found a box of old toys, including a bunch of Fraggle dolls that I had as a kid. When I mentioned this to my sister, she said she heard that Fraggles were making a comeback with a new movie coming out. Sure enough, when I checked Amazon, the complete series was available. Some of them are actually a bit tender. The episodes often deal with themes like prejudice and the environment.

That being said, I'd recommend getting the newer [[ASIN:B002LYD2LW Fraggle Rock: Complete Series Collection]] DVD set. It has the complete series (as opposed to just a few episodes as on this product). For the price, it's a steal. I hope you enjoy your time "down in Fraggle Rock"!

review_title: DON'T PUT THIS ON YOUR REGISTRY
review_text:
I am a loyal Amazon customer. I have been a Prime member for years and so when it was time for my (now) husband and I to make a registry for our wedding, Amazon was an obvious option. As I searched through all the options of things to put on the registry, this popped up as a suggestion. My husband and I both work multiple jobs and money is always tight, so I figured if we were given this as a gift, it would be a nice excuse to get away for a weekend. Well, it turns out if people contribute money towards this in your registry, you don't actually get the gift cards. You are just given credit to Amazon. After 1 email, 2 different people on messenger, and 4 different people on the phone I was told it is illegal to use group gifting contributions on Amazon for a gift card to something else. When I said to the man "this makes no sense, why was this Massanutten gift card even an option then?" his response was "well, your guest got a pop-up box explicitly explaining the federal laws." I could be wrong but I think most times when we see a picture of a gift card and a title saying "Massanutten Gift Card" people think it is generally straight forward. Well, it's not.

Now if it is the case that all of this was because I had the group gifting tab checked to on, then my question is: why would amazon even allow that to be an option on gift cards to other places? Needless to say, the money my husband I and were going to use to take make step-son snow tubing is now sitting in my Amazon credit balance and I am unable to use it for Massanutten.

I hope this helps someone else out there before they make the same mistake I did because let me tell you, customer service will not help you.

review_title: large washcloth sized felt like fabric, add water for light lather. Then towel dry off
review_text:
How this fits into your life depends on what you need. It still requires some water, and still requires toweling off. It basically replaces the need to have a separate low suds cleansing formula and wash rag or dry cloth. THIS IS Rinse free, but you do need water to start. Just add a little water to the sheet of fabric, massage for light lather, wipe down body, then towel off. No need to rinse. Keep in mind that the more water that is used, the more the mess from run off.

The sheet of fabric is like a soft piece of felt. Size of a large washcloth (9.5" x 9.5"). Don't need much water! It definitely lathers. It isn't a sudsy soap, but that doesn't mean there isn't enough. Now, if you are expecting loads of foamy bubbles, this does not provide that. It creates a light watery lather. This in no way determines effectiveness of cleaning. Mega lather does not equate better cleaning. I learned that 30 some years ago in home economics that excess lather is a marketing technique (usually through copious amounts of sulphates) to give people impression that more lather/bubbles/suds = better clean (shampoo, body soaps, toothpaste). But for those that dig the suds, I can get some light bubbles out of it. That being said, it is adequate enough. Not super refreshing, but I do feel clean. Tried it in hair with fair results.

This could be cut in half and it would still have plenty of lather. Depending on your situation, this could be premoistened and placed in a ziplock baggie.

No discernable aroma. Not sticky, at least not me. I wonder if amount of water used, or thoroughness of toweling off impacts that or not.

Personally, I prefer wet body wipes. They never need water nor toweling off. I like those for on the go use (workday, after work out, bird bath at the sink). I would be more apt to use these in a bed bound situation, or no hot water situation, maybe camping.

The term "waterless" needs to be taken out from the title headline. That is a traffic directing manipulation, and it helps no one especially if they buy something like this without further looking at the product pictures and description.

This type of cleaning format is outstanding for resource conservation. It comes in sheets that dissolve far more readily and quickly than the tablet format concentrates. The sheets are easy to cut (or tear) if you need a smaller amount for the task.

While these sheets are positioned as a floor cleaner (and it works pretty well for that task) they can also be used as a general purpose spray cleaner. I use a sheet for a 32oz bottle, and the spray does a fine job for counters, sinks, and other general cleaning tasks. The scent is reasonably pleasant, but I would have preferred no scent as other sheets offer.

There are some cons, however. First, the cost is higher than similar sheet-based concentrates, and the performance is no different than the lower cost options. Second, the packaging is not ideal for sheets. The sheets are somewhat delicate and must be kept totally dry in storage or they will dissolve. The sheets are packaged in a cardboard box in a single clump. Other manufacturers use a plastic box or, if a cardboard box is used, the sheets are divided up into smaller groups.

Factoring in the cons puts my score at 3 stars. Although the sheet format is perfect for eliminating plastic waste and is easier to use than the tablet-based format, there are better sheet options available at a lower price.

Motif Medical: Motif Twist

The twist is a small, lightweight very portable breast pump. It comes with a 24mm one piece breast flange with a comfort cushion. It can be battery operated with four AA batteries. It is rather cute in appearance to me and it comes with a one year warranty. Replacement parts can be hard to get if one is attempting to order direct however aeroflowbreastpumps.com carries Motif Medical replacement parts. The pump comes with no accessories. If you need a tote and cooler you’ll have to purchase your own. Warranty on the pump is one year from date of purchase or received through insurance.

What’s included…
♦ 4 Valves and membranes,
♦ 2 Wide neck bottles (ML volume only) with nipples and hard plastic sealing disc
♦ 2 One piece flanges with comfort cushions & caps (Flanges included is the standard 24mm only)
♦ 1 AC Power Adapter
♦ 2 Sets of tubing

PROS…
♦ Twist is a closed pump, meaning there is a barrier usually a diaphragm that prevents milk and condensation from entering the tubing
♦ Small and lightweight which makes for high portability. It’s far lighter than my Avent double electric comfort pump and that too is far lighter than other double electric pumps.
♦ Parts is interchangeable with the Motif Curve
♦ Flanges is rather light in comparison to other full one piece bodies
♦ Comfort cushion makes for one of the most comfortable pumping experiences
♦ Twist has two phase expression. When the pump is turned on it starts in the let-down phase where it replicates the faster suckling a baby would do to get milk flowing. Turning the dial up enters the expression phase. When expressing I noted that higher suction has a longer pull on the nipple.
♦ With some hacks flanges/flange bodies can be used from other closed pumps
♦ Other bottles than can be pumped into is Avent classic/natural and Dr. Browns wide neck bottle (This is only if using motif flanges)
♦ Twist is a double electric pump allowing mom to express from both breast at the same time

CONS…
♦ Pump is loud. It’s comparable to Avent Double Electric Comfort Pump in terms of loudness.
♦ Motif only carries a 24mm flange and a 28mm flange.
♦ Parts is hard to get. At this time what I noted is only Aeroflowbreastpumps.com carrying all of Motif replacement parts.
♦ One must use Motif brand valves and membranes or duckbill valves. The flange opening where the valve would go is far smaller than Medela so trying to use Medela valve/membranes or third party ones from Nene Supply/Mayomom will not work with the Motif Twist flanges.
♦ Tubing is double ended which forces a lactating mom to use Motif parts. ( I did a hack and cut one of the ends off allowing for me to use flange/flange bodies from other companies. I also noted that the tubing is rather soft and has some stretch to it, allowing for me to remove the excess plastic from the end for use with Spectra tubing. Thus far I was able to use my Avent comfort flanges and my Medela personal fit connectors with Pumpin’Pals flanges with the Motif Twist. < Most commercial, single user breast pumps use vacuum technology so flanges can be used interchangeably between brands.>)
♦ ( This is a personal con which may not be across the board for all moms.) Vaccum sucks the nipple and areola in well and creates good suction. I noted this phenomenon between three different company flanges where removing the flange from the breast is a bit of a task and has sort of a pop like noise from the release. I don’t have this feeling when using electric breast pumps from other companies.
♦ Motif Medical only has Monday through Friday customer service from 8am-5pm EST.

Update 1/7/2018

I called Motif’s customer service asking about replacement parts and a larger flange size. Please understand that cutting the tubing to use different company flanges can and will void out your warranty. Parts is covered for 3m and motor is one year according to the warranty. I was informed that a 32mm flange is in the works and should be available soon this year. I was sent two 28mm flanges and extra valve/membranes. Although I have been using size 30mm flanges for most of my pumping career, I recently changed out to size 28mm to note that I am able to express well with the size. 30mm may be more comfortable for me to use with no chances of my nipple hitting the back of the flanges.

Motif has an interesting flange for size 28mm. The body and flange is separate from each other. The diaphragms, I noted is bigger than what is included with the 24mm flange. It’s a small pot and is far deeper than the 24mm ones. 24mm Flange has a shallow pot diaphragm. The flange is also shaped like a pot. It covers all of my areola and is quite comfortable. It’s far more comfortable than Medela in my opinion. I also decided to change valves from the two piece valve/membrane thing most companies put out. I switched to a third party duckbill valve from NeneSupply also sold on Amazon and noted that it fits onto the flanges and work well. The valve/membrane combination doesn’t offer good suction thus I need a higher vacuum to express with. Maymom another third party after market retailer also sold on Amazon carries a thread changer which also works well with Motif flanges. With the thread changer I was able to express into Medela and Ameda narrow neck bottles just fine. The thread changer only works properly with duckbill valves that aren’t Avent. ( Avent style valves one cannot express with using the thread. ) Thread also works well with the two piece valve/membrane combination.

Overall, I would recommend the Twist. It’s a high quality pump and I personally respond to it well. Flanges are quite comfortable to use and the pump is extremely light weight. The pump is rather loud but it’s no louder than other pumps close to its size. Replacement parts may be hard to obtain but Aeroflow carries them as well as a call to customer service one can get them. Third party duckbill valves work with motif flanges and the 28mm flanges is easy to clean.

Update 3/7/2018

I recently went looking for replacement parts only to note that 1. Motif updated their website to include a parts store 2. The 28mm flange was updated. 32 is still not available, neither is a full flange size 21mm or 19mm. Currently the insert for the 24mm flange reduces the flange down to a 21mm. There is an insert for the 28mm flange however I was informed via customer service that it's only for added comfort and it doesn't change the flange size.

The 28mm flange is now a single, one piece body, with a shallow pot diaphragm. It was changed as I was told the old version was more expensive to produce than the current model. The new 28mm flange has a very similar appearance to the 24mm flange included with the pump. I have yet to receive and use the new model but I shall soon and update this review again.

Update 3/27/2018

I recently called Motif customer service. As my pump is still under warranty for parts I inquired about the 28mm flanges. I was sent another set of flanges though with shipping one of my flanges arrived broken. It's no big deal as the original set I was sent is still functioning just fine. Motif has not changed their 28mm flanges. It's still a two piece item with a larger pot diaphragm. The parts store shows a replacement diaphragm being the same size as it is for the 24mm flange. From what I am seeing via photos and what originally came with my pump the 24mm flange body has a shallower pot for the diaphragm. Parts store claims the flanges both 24mm and 28mm use the same size diaphragm but such is not the case as one is far bigger than the other. There is still no other flange size out side of 24mm and 28mm. 28mm Flange now has an insert I have not used nor ordered as the flange is very comfortable to use.

Still I would recommend the pump for mamas who use the available flange sizes. It's still a high quality pump and I believe it performs far better than my Spectra s2 and my Medela pisa ( pump in style advance.) Customer service is good and Motif makes quality breast pumps.

Update 09/12/2018
I recently noted that Motif Medical has taken to offering their replacement parts and flanges on Amazon. We can not order breast flange kits with valves/membranes and tubing included. Breast flange inserts, replacement valves/membranes, diaphragms, extra flanges and so on is now sold on here making it convenient to get parts.

My pump now being 8m old is currently in the process of being replaced. After doing routine maintenance of replacing tubing, duckbills ( I don't respond well to the valve/membrane combo so I don't use them ) and diaphragms monthly, I noted that my pump is no longer able to provide me with adequate suction even when increasing the suction on the pump. With daily use of three plus times a day it is past it's prime. As with other pumps I've replaced in the past, the old motor will be sent back in exchange for the new motor. I never used the pump as a double as for me I noted that it doesn't perform well as such. I always used my pump as a single and on AC power, never battery. Using any pump as a double kills the vacuum strength thus motor is worked harder and mom would need to use higher suction overall. I would still recommend this pump for moms on the go now that parts is easier to get and the fact the pump is reasonably priced even when it's on sale.

review_title: Update:  Great side effect: No more snoring!
review_text:
Update to my review from 2009:
I have found the same product for much cheaper at my local Costco: a bottle of Kirkland "Mucus Relief Chest Guaifenesin 400 mg, 200 tablets" for $11.55 ($0.06/400 mg tablet) instead of this ProHealth product of 100 tablets for ~$20 ($0.20/400 mg tablet). The ProHealth is over 3 times the price! And the Kirkland brand tablets are MUCH easier to swallow.

The price at my local Costco is currently cheaper, btw, than buying the same Kirkland bottle on amazon (http://www.amazon.com/Kirkland-Signature-Expectorant-Guaifenesin-Immediate-Release/dp/B002RL8FIE/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&s=hpc&qid=1291354212&sr=1-1)

======================

First, my product review

Pros:
- Eliminates my snoring! (see below, your mileage will vary)
- The least expensive product (per mg) that I have found so far.
- Shipping has been reliable from this vendor.
- Product is 100% guaifenesin (no decongestent, etc..)

Cons
- As previously posted by another reviewer, they can be difficult to swallow because of their size and the fact they are not coated. I have a large mouth :) so not so much a problem for me, but those with smaller mouths/throats (like my wife) might have more difficulty.

I have been taking Guaifenesin for the last 5+ years. My allergy doctor recommends taking it when I first notice allergy or cold symptoms as a means to help me combat the allergy/cold and recuperate faster.

I used to snore often and thought I had sleep apnea (I don't, according to an overnight sleep study). My wife and I were both sleeping poorly from my snoring and our quality of life was greatly impacted. She made this (life-saving!) observation that I did not snore when I was on the guaifenesin when I was taking it for cold/allergy symptoms.

Given how guaifenesin is rated as a relatively safe drug, my allergy doctor saw no harm in taking it regularly and told me that, although it is not advertised to help address snoring, he could see how thinning the mucus (that I often have) would make breathing through my air passage easier and reduce the snoring.

Guaifenesin might not help your snoring at all, but I would certainly recommend that you talk to your doctor if you have a snoring problem and ask if it makes sense to try it.

Let's face it, hot flashes are not fun. I started peri-menopause last year and the hot flashes started to ramp up a few months ago. Getting old is an interesting journey.

I have used a lot of different icepacks and they work, but none of them really seem to help solve the problem. This pack feels different. I wear it over a t-shirt and usually under a thin sweatshirt or fleece. Typically I wear it in the evening before I go to bed because I find that if I cool my temperature off at night I sleep better.

I have found that if I keep this pack in the freezer I can use it for a little over an over and it does stay really cold. It is not overwhelmingly cold, but it is comfortingly cold. The claim that it pulls heat away from your body is really true. There is no other way to describe it. It is the strangest feeling to suddenly feel like your body temperature is dropping. It is pleasant.

The one drawback is the cost. At $139, I am not sure what makes this that much better than two very large gel ice packs other than the shape. Unless I had unlimited amounts of money I am not sure I would spend that much.

I live in Michigan where the temperature is starting to get colder, but I know that next summer I will be using the heck out of this pack.

review_text:
My eyes are extremely dry and I struggle at night. I use a very thick eye lotion -sounds weird, but it helps- and eye masks help to keep me from rubbing my eyes at night. I have found some eye masks are better than others.

The masks I really like are the super soft masks that cover most of the top of my face. I have also found the masks that irritate my eyes the most are the super soft masks that cover most of the top of my face. They work really well, but for some reason, they aggravate my eyes a lot.

This mask, first of all, blocks all the light. When I put it on it is completely dark. It is easy to adjust and it is comfortable. It is all black with no design, so it is a simple and appropriate grown up sleep mask.

I hand washed it before I used it and hung it on the line to dry before I first used it and it dried within a couple hours. Simple. I wash my masks once or twice a week because my eyes are very sensitive.

This mask is firm, but comfortable. It did not cut into my face and after a little adjustment was easy to sleep with. I did wake up with sleep mask face, but I always wake up with sleep mask face. This mask, I noticed, gives my eyes some breathing room, which is so nice because I put my drops in and then stick my mask on and having a mask pressing against wet eyes is never pleasant.

I like this mask and for the price is one I could easily have a few of to rotate around while I wash them to protect my eyes while I sleep.

After reading through a number of other descriptions and reviews of this same product, I discovered that the full-size syringes I was accustomed to are 2.4 ml, and those products that offer this size specifically say so. If the description doesn't tell you what size the syringe is, you can and should assume it's the really small size. This product is the really small size.

And don't fall for the repackaging of this product that they're now calling ZOOM. Actually, don't fall for the packaging they show you of any of them, because that's not what you'll necessarily get, as many reviewers have noted, and now they "mention" this might occur in the description, too.

What they don't tell you, is that some of this product is counterfeit and doesn't work at all. That's why you see some reviews from really unhappy customers - it's not them, they received a counterfeit product. The company that fulfilled the ZOOM I got was SmileMedic, and I wouldn't trust them ever again, and neither should you.

When I called Amazon about it, they couldn't have been nicer about it and refunded my money immediately. I offered to send the rest of it back so they could have it tested to prove that it's counterfeit, because Amazon doesn't need to get the reputation for selling counterfeit products. Until they get this straightened out with SmileMedic, I suggest you save yourself the grief and don't buy anything from that company, and if the stuff you get from anyone else is counterfeit too, let Amazon know.

UPDATE:
I found these made my shoes MUCH too tight as the insoles that came in the shoes couldn't be removed. I have put them in my rubber boots, having been able to remove those insoles, which was about the same thickness as these at the front end, and they are really comfortable. I think I'll be using the half insoles in future as they seem to suit my shoes better.
ORIGINAL REVIEW:
I use orthotic insoles in all my shoes, even my slippers, to alleviate some of the pain of arthritis in my foot joints. I have several half-insole Rooruns and have worn out several Walk-fits. So, when I saw these in my "Recommended for you" list as an Amazon Vine Reviewer, I thought they are worth trying. As a Vine Reviewer, I was able to order these at no cost to me, in exchange for an objective and detailed review.
Here it is...
The construction is typical of Rooruns, with various layers of material to provide comfort and support. I do wish they were stiffer or were flat on the bottom, as they tend to bend under foot, losing some of the free shape, especially if the shoe has no arch support profile. That said, they do provide noticeable support in flat shoes. Also, the Rooruns I have do not lose their shape with repeated use and are very durable. The half-insole one in the photo has been in my shoes for some time now, with little sign of wear. My slippers' insoles have the most wear and that's a fading of the fabric color, the upper fabric layer has worn down under the heel (but not peeled, just worn) and the heel cushion/pad is starting to come loose. However, the slippers have the most hours on them, several hours a day over several months with the typical lack of support to stop the foot sliding around. I expect these full insoles to perform just as well. That is one key feature which draws me to Roorun insoles - durability.
The arch profile is definitely higher than my other Rooruns and I have high arches, so that felt good under my feet.
I ordered the XL for my size 13 feet. On the floor, the insoles seemed much longer than my feet and I was thinking I would need to cut the front ends down. There are molded-in lines underneath to suggest where and how to cut. However, when I tried to put them in my loafers, I found that forcing them over the top of the heel, down into the actually-longer sole area of the shoe, they fit my size 13 shoes perfectly. They do reduce volume inside the shoe, especially in the heel area. I measured them at approx. 3/8" thick at the heel, but that's the same as my half-insoles. The extra material under the toes, which I'm not used to, did make my shoes feel a little tighter at the front and top.
Interestingly, the round heel cushion/pad under the insole has a plastic film over it. Remove the film and the pad is very sticky. Presumably to retain its position in the shoe. Now why would you need that on the full insole when it's trapped front and rear in position, yet the half-insoles do not have it, and actually would stay put better with it?!
The half-insoles often slip forward when I put shoes or boots on.
ROORUN: PLEASE NOTE: I wish that sticky pad feature was on the half-insoles!
The price is competitive and only $6 or so more than the half insoles. I still think I prefer the half insoles, but the higher arch might be better for me. We will see.
I haven't had a chance to wear these for an extended time. I will get that chance this coming weekend on a trip. I'll update the review after I get more miles with these insoles.

review_title: Works well; arrived super quickly; needs better description
review_text:
I was looking for one-way straws for my mother, who is quadriplegic, so that when she drinks the liquid will stay in the straw. However, every one-way straw I found had a diameter too wide for her preference. These select flow valves were our best shot at being able to have our desired effect on the straws she presently uses. I saw these first on the ARK website. There, they have the option to buy in packs of 3 and up. However, this listing on amazon does not outline how many you will receive for the price. I needed them quickly; so, I bit the bullet and purchased them, as a prime member, not knowing how many would arrive for the price. I was pleasantly surprised to find 3 were sent for my purchase price (which I believe was just under $8, including shipping). I was also pleasantly surprised by how quickly they arrived. I selected two-day shipping, but these arrived at my door the next day - and early in the morning! Kudos!

In order to fit well on a straw, the straws diameter should be at least 3/16" wide. My mother uses a more narrow straw (1/8"), and as such these valves to do not fit well. Again, how they are used and how large the device is is not outlined in the product description. Instructions for use are provided in the packaging, but it would be nice to see in the product's description before buying.

Having said all of that, they do work well and for their intended purpose provided the straw is large enough, and again, the shipping was super fast!

review_title: Good quality - Comfortable fit - Great price
review_text:
The 5-pack of Blue Blocking Half Frame Reading Glasses from Louol Readers is a good way to have several identical magnification power reading glasses handy in different locations at a very reasonable price (averaging just $4 per pair at the time of this review). Note that while the power is the same in all 5 pairs, the frame color of each pair is different.
As for blue-blocking, I really can’t determine if these reading glasses actually block any specific wavelength of light. Maybe they do, maybe they don’t. Looking at the edge of the lenses it certainly appears that there is a thin layer of something pressed in between 2 thicker layers of the actual lens material (polycarbonate?) . I can observe a blue tinted reflection of light while holding the glasses under any bright light bulb while my regular (not blue-blocking) glasses do not show any blue tinting.
As for comfort these glasses hit the mark, very comfortable on the bridge of the nose and the flex of the spring hinge hold the glasses onto the face without putting too much pressure on the temples. Overall quality seems really good and the frames are just as fashionable as most name brand frames.
While I feel that the reading glasses themselves are really good, the packaging and packing are concerning. The 5 pairs of glasses are in a very lightweight box with zero padding and the shipping container used by Amazon is a basic soft bag so the product box can be easily crushed during handling and as a result some or all pairs of glasses could get damaged. As seen in 2 of the photos below, the product box was partially crushed although I was fortunate and none of the glasses were damaged. This could certainly be a real issue and something that the manufacturer/packager should consider.

I think that supplementing for bone health is very important, especially for women as they age. The prevalence of osteoporosis is very high amongst aging women and men. Oftentimes your doctor will recommend taking calcium, but I find that calcium on it's own can be overdone in some instances. I do like that this supplement contains vitamin K, because vitamin K is known to help in calcium absorbency. I found the pills to be on the large side, but I didn't have any difficulty swallowing them. I will say that taking them 4 times a day is a little cumbersome, and not really something that I would continue to do. What I normally do when it comes to supplementation, is cut whatever the recommendation is that I'm giving in half. So in my case, I decided to do one pill twice a day. I took one before breakfast and one before dinner. It was recommended to take these with a meal, and as I normally take the rest of my supplements without a meal I decided to take their advice, and take this one with food. That being said, I did notice a tinge of an after taste. I wouldn't say that it was terribly pleasant, but at the same time I guess because I ate after having taken it, it certainly lessen the effects. I never tried it without a meal, but if that's what I could taste with a meal, I don't think I'd recommend taking this pill on its own. All in all, it's a good supplement to include as far as increasing your bone density perhaps through supplementation. The price seems very reasonable to me, and I think it's worth a recommendation. review_title: Solves BlackWidow Keyboard Problem of No Backlighting for Upper Case Symbols
review_text:
These RAZER DOUBLESHOT PBT KEYCAPS (for Mechanical & Optical Keyboards: Compatible with Standard 104/105 US and UK layouts; Razer Green) work great with my Razer BlackWidow Ultimate keyboard. I have always loved the keyboard, because it’s so customizable, but have hated the lack of keycap backlighting for the uppercase symbols. I’m a touch typist, but have a bad habit of peeking at the number keys to get the uppercase symbols.

As you can see from my photo, these keycaps solve the problem. By placing the number and symbol labels side by side at the top, both are properly backlit. You do have to remember that the label on the left is for the lower case (usually a number) key, but that’s easy to do.

It’s too bad that the keycaps for the BlackWidow Ultimate keyboard weren’t designed like this in the first place. The box of keycaps comes with a keycap puller, as well as with stabilizers for the larger keys. The instructions are very easy to understand, and swapping out the keycaps is a simple job.

review_title: My Headphone Fanatic VERY PICKY Kids Love These
review_text:
I originally got these headphones with the thought that I could play my playstation with them. Unfortunately, I forgot that you can not use headphones with a PS3. So, my kids got to try these. Let's take a look.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These headphones are really nicely designed. My daughter said they are brilliantly designed. The top that goes on top of your head is very stretchy and the wire part about it is one position.

MICROPHONE
The microphone is not retractable, but folds out of place if you want it to. It lights up when it is in use, and when it is disabled, it is not lit. The mic is clear and very loud. It is easy to control.

EARPHONE PADS
The pads are very comfortable and cushioned well. We can wear these a while before they have to be taken off. It is quite comfortable to all of us who tried these on. They are not leather, so if you have sweaty ears, you might have to remove them for a bit now and then.

CONTROLS
The controls on the left ear are all in the back. They are difficult to control unless I take off the headset. However, one of the kids has no problem doing it with them on. I guess it depends but either way, it is not difficult.

CORD
The cord is only about 6ft long which means you can not sit very far away from your PC or gaming machine, unless you have an extension you can add to it, which I suggest you get prior to purchase.

LIGHTS
The lights on these are really cool. They are colorful and can be turned off if you want. If you have a keyboard or gaming pad that has lights on it, these will go well with them.

SOUND QUALITY
When used with PC games, the sound quality of these is really nice. The kids love the sound, nice base, vibration is decent, and the separation of the sounds is great. Even without the drivers installed, it worked really well. My kids are VERY critical and picky, so for them to rave about these is significant.

DOES THIS WORK WITH PS3?
If you have a lot of USB ports on your TV you might be able to use these with your PS3 through the TV but not use the mic as that has to be put in a different way. If not, then it won't work with the PS3 although you can use the mic, just not hear the sound effects through the headphones.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These headphones are excellent for PC gaming and if you can get them to work with PS3 or PS4. The sound separation is great, the 3D is nice and even without the drivers on the CDROM included, the headphones work well.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. For the price, these have been a surprise for our family. The PC gaming is really nice with them, and if I can get my PS3 hooked up to a TV with USB ports, perhaps I can make it work for that in the future. For now, I am content to play PC games with these, if I can get them away from the kids, that is.

review_title: One of the best prebuilt keyboards available.
review_text:
I just purchased this and have not owned it for long, but I was anxious to type at length. The main reasons I purchased this board were for it's hotswap capabilities as well as the low profile/zero tilt case. For some reason flat enthusiast mechanical keyboards are almost unheard of. I have lower profile board in space gray, with Halo Clear switches.

Keycaps- The keycaps are certainly better than average, and they better be for the cost of this board. I prefer PBT- I like the harder material, the sound, and the rougher texture. However, these are almost too rough- they are gritty like sandpaper. My favorite keycaps are Leopold. Just to compare the keycaps on the Anne Pro II are also PBT, but they are pretty smooth and not ideal. I like the font and the shine through legends. On two sides they measure 1.33mm and the other two 1.01. I'm not sure why they are not even all around. The are OEM profile and have a pleasant sound. I may replace them, but am not rushing to do so.

Switches- This board has Halo Clears, though there are about 1/2 dozen other choices available. These are rated at 63 grams I believe, but they bottom out at 80 grams. They are heavy. The are smooth and have good tactility- and I like the force curve. They all ping like crazy however which annoys the heck out of me. I like these a lot, but I will be swapping the springs out for lighter ones. There is minimal switch wobble, but I think the heavier springs help to mitigate some of that.

Case- the case is flat and low profile which I like. It is aluminum which I'm neutral about. I'm perfectly fine with plastic and the metal adds cost to the whole package. This is a "floating switch" design, meaning the bottom of the switches are exposed. I used to like this, but I actually prefer the more tradition kind where the bezel covers the base of the switch. The case has zero tilt which was my number one requirement. It comes with magnetic feet which are quite sturdy and raise the incline about 4-5 degrees. There are recessed hole the feet go into and the case can even be declined. Don't worry they are not coming off if you slide the board. I actually had a really difficult time getting them off after I attached them.

RGB- These can be adjusted using FN plus various letters and there are controls for brightness, breathing, color, scrolling pattern, etc. I don't know if there is more fine tuning control when you flash the firmware (I just use a dim backlight). There is also RGB going around the base of the case which I turn off.

Stabilizers- I can detect just a slight rattle in the space bar, but I think the heavier springs help to prevent some vibration. I have read that the stabs are not very good so I have already purchased new ones and will be installing them tomorrow.

Software/Programmability- I have not experimented with this yet. There is a process to flash the firmware for the layout you desire. I would remap the Fn to the CapsLock and then the arrows to I,J,K,L.

Overall Value- $200 dollars is a lot of money for a keyboard. At this price point you can just about build the board yourself and choose the components. I would have chosen different switches (though I'm really starting to like these) and a plastic case which would have saved money, and different keycaps. However, I paid $140 for this new on eBay and I feel at this price it is a great value. Ultimately it was the flat case that made me pull the trigger. I have heard of people complaining about the rattling stabilizers which they felt should not happen at this price point.

I should also point out that there may be some issues with the USB-C cable. Some cables are not compatible- I believe they need to be rated for 2.4a, and not just data. I will say that my own USB- Cable would not even fit in the port which was strange- I did not force it. For people who like to use the fancy coiled cables they may not work.

Included in the case is a switch puller, keycap puller, and the feet. The are all wedged in the foam base.

I had some older joy-cons that had drift issues and worn down joysticks. I figured that I didn't have anything to lose by replacing them myself. I had already replaced the joy-cons with newer ones. I will say that it isn't the easiest thing to replace the joysticks, but with minimal knowledge and patience, you can do it. The kit comes with 4 joysticks along with all of the tools in the picture. I used every piece of the kit except for the extra screws and two joysticks.

To start, you need to use the star screwdriver to open up the joy-con casing. Once all four screws are out, you need to get the pieces of casing separated using the guitar pick. Be careful to not disconnect anything and set aside pieces as you get into the insides of the controller. Once you have the casing separated, you need to get under the battery. There is one to three phillips head screws (depending on left or right joycon) holding a plastic piece that holds the battery for the controller. Once you have the plastic piece holding the battery off, you will see the circuit board for the controller. Carefully remove the joystick using the screwdriver and tweezers. You will need to disconnect the cord coming off of it. Once you pop the joystick out, you just need to put the new one in the same was and connect the cord to the controller! After that, you just need to reassemble your controller and test it out!

The joysticks work perfectly, and I have had no issues with them so far. I still have two back-up ones to replace my current main controllers if needed! I highly recommend this kit.

review_title: Pickup is weak, sound field is amazing
review_text:
It comes with a USB cable to update the controller. I found that odd, but convenient. I can always use extra cables. The adapter has controls to increase game sounds, increase chat sounds, mute the microphone (it lights up if the mike is muted--a very convenient feature) and it can turn up and down the volume as a whole. The audio cable is standard, so you can use it in anything else that works with a headphone. The microphone retracts well enough to be invisible if you don't know to look for it. I used it for a bit with my 3DS and it worked fine for that. The audio cable is permanently attached, and I do not like that design choice. The cable is the single most likely part to break (worse for me because my cat chews these cables, but true in general). A port with a swappable cable would increase the lifespan of these headphones, and would offer choices in terms of swapping to a longer cable, a shorter cable. A more modular design is always a better choice.

It's a good size for a female. The microphone is well places (more on that in a bit) and the headset fits well and is comfortable. It's lightweight, comfortable, and easy to wear for long gaming sessions. The padding was soft without being annoying or sweaty. The ear cups don't annoy the ears the way some can after a long while.

As I said, the microphone sits well. It sits exactly where other headsets I have used sits. For me at least, position isn't a problem. The problem is that the pickup is lacking. If I speak at a normal level--and here I admit to being fairly soft spoken-- it doesn't fully pick up my voice. It echoes in the headset, and does that very well. It reminds me of the studio setup I had back when I was podcasting It's that kind of quality echo back. That's my largest issue with these, and the reason they lose a star. They might have gone to three stars but for the sound field.

The sound field is astounding. I had to keep taking the headset off to see if I was really hearing through the headset and not the speakers. The sounds are directional and adequately distant to give the audio illusion of space and positions in space. I have never heard audio this good from headsets in this price range. That's where this headset truly shines. The sound quality, the range of base and treble, and the sound clarity is impressive as well. In fact, if you're looking for a set so that you can watch shows or play without the noise bothering anyone else, and the mike isn't an issue (or if you naturally have a loud voice) you are going to be hard pressed to find anything better than these.

review_title: You won't have fun playing this game
review_text:
After playing this game for a few week (and well as several month with the previous version) the only rational conclusion I can make is the creators of the game hate you and do not want you to have fun playing this game. The game's AI players are so hard to beat that you'll never progress very far in career mode. Here's the "fun" you can expect from this game when trying to beat the AI:

* Your stamina will quickly fade, sometime by as much as 50% after a few points. The AI players will always have more stamina, and, therefore, can hit hard, powerful shots at will any time in the game with little loss of stamina.
* Some points you will lose no mater what you do, as if the point was predetermined before you started. Even lower ranked players will enter the "god mode" during a point, and will be absolutely unbeatable. You'll end up losing the point and nearly all your stamina in the process.
* AI players do not make errors very often. In this version, they make about 98% of their shots. They can also cover the court and hit perfect shots at will. You may get good and manage to get winners about one out of 100 times. Sure, you'l get plenty of opportunities to hit winners, but you'f find they almost always land in the middle of the court, easy returnable.
* There's a whole slew of confusing achievement cards that get unlocked, good luck finding out how they improve your player in any meaningful way, for example "power increased 5% but control decreased by 8%"

Sure, this isn't Mario tennis. It's Dark Souls. Nobody asked for this.

review_title: VR Is Not Just For Kids.  Everyone Should Have One of These!
review_text:
I’m truly amazed at how awesome this Occulus Quest 2 refurbished headset is. It’s the same as the Meta Quest 2, but it has the old logo on it. It’s also discounted about $50, which is why I decided to finally try VR. I don’t know why I waited so long! Oh, I know, most of us probably think VR is just for kids, or we don’t like shooting games, or we get motion sick and all that jumping around would be too much for us. I know, that as someone who’s considered, well elderly, I should just stay away from this nonsense and leave it to grandkids, right? That is so wrong! Sure, there’s a lot of violent shooting games available and you could easily make yourself sick riding roller coasters in VR, and there’s a lot of potential for people to abuse community spaces and bully others, but that’s just a tiny portion of what VR opens up to you when you put on a Quest 2 headset. I’m the first to admit, I had my reservations, but although I’m old, and disabled to boot, I don’t think you ever get too old to try something new, especially something like this that lets you experience things that you’ve never experienced, without having to leave the comfort of your home. You don’t have to climb mountains in VR, but with this headset you can if you want to. You can come pretty close to the experience without actually plummeting towards the earth when you jump and miss your handholds. The view are spectacular in that particular game, but I had to return it because although it says you can play it sitting, I couldn’t really do it from a wheelchair. That’s not a problem, though, because if you purchase most games or apps you have the option to return it within 14 days, providing you haven’t spent over a certain amount of time using it. But there’s plenty that even someone as limited in physical ability as I am can enjoy in VR, thanks to this fully self contained headset. With the Quest 2, you don’t need to be tethered to an expensive gaming computer, and there are things that anyone can find in VR that will amaze and astonish even the most unflappable person. Right now, there are a wide variety of games and apps, some free, that no matter your age or interests, you will be able to find things that make you say, “Wow!”. You can get an app that allows you to go anywhere in the world, similar to using Google Earth, except that you find yourself being able to look around as if you were there at a famous landmark or your childhood home. You can take guided tours to places you probably didn’t know existed, or take a tour of the Space Station and see how the astronauts live and work there, go swimming with whales or watch gorillas play in a jungle. You can meditate, play musical instruments, meet people with similar interests, take courses, draw and paint in 2D and 3D, play golf or dance, surf the internet, or one of my favorite things so far, sit in a movie theater and get the feeling of truly watching a movie on a big screen while actually being comfortable at home. I know that sounds unusual, but for someone like me who hasn’t been able to go to a movie theater in many years, it’s a truly awesome experience. I haven’t had my Quest 2 long enough yet, to convince friends and family to join me in VR, but if they do, we can watch movies or play games together in a variety of settings. For me, the neatest game I’ve discovered yet is VR Fishing! It’s so relaxing to fish in real places in Japan, South Korea, or the Northwestern USA, in a variety of weather conditions, from shore or in boats, and to catch fish and put them in your Aquarium in your fish lodge. It’s a nearly magical experience to feel as if you are truly getting a nibble to catching a fish that looks so real that you can forget for a moment that you’re at home, and you feel like you’re actually sitting in a wooden boat in the rain and mist at a lake in the mountains. VR is awesome for everyone, but especially if you or someone you know loves to travel or fish, or do any number of things but you find yourself unable to enjoy such activities anymore due to physical limitations or even monetary restrictions. VR is a great way to expand possibilities beyond what’s easily available. If I were younger and healthier, my dream job would be to bring VR to as many people as possible, but especially to elderly and home bound or disabled folks whose lives are getting narrower and restricted. VR can expand your environment in ways that have never been possible before. Quest 2 is relatively affordable, easy to use, and it will only get better as more people expand their lives into the VR environment. I was surprised at how easy it was get started, and I was able to do most of it right from within VR. Is it perfect? Absolutely not. It’s a bit of a money pit. When you buy the Quest 2, you get a headset, two controllers, and a charger cord. That’s all. The controllers are battery powered. If you want rechargeable controllers, you’ll likely need a charger base with rechargeable batteries. You’ll almost certainly have to get a head strap because the one that comes with the Quest 2 headset is minimal and it feels like the headset is going to fall off no matter how much you tighten it when you put it on. If you want to balance it better and give you more playtime, you’ll need a head strap with a battery. Unless you invest in a charging station, you’ll probably want a case, and lens covers because you can’t allow sunlight to hit the the lenses because that could burn out headset. There are other helpful accessories, such as controller covers, lens cloths and covers, possibly a fan to keep your glasses from fogging if you wear glasses, or you can buy prescription lenses here on Amazon, or other accessories. Some are more necessary than others, and depending of what you use your headset for, you may not need every possible accessory. At this moment, as fun as VR is, it’s still in it’s infancy, but it’s usefulness to others besides video gamers is growing every day. Meta Quest 2 is probably the most useful and affordable stand alone VR system available, and there’s plenty to be found in it. I’ve barely scratched the surface of what it’s capable of doing, and I think that even old folks like me, who might be initially reluctant to try it, can find plenty of awesome things to do if we can be persuaded to try it out. I’m kicking myself that I didn’t buy one the first time I saw it, because it would have made my pandemic isolation a lot less isolating. I wish that something like this would have been available when my dad was confined to bed and a wheelchair after his stroke many years ago, because he loved to travel and learn new things, and VR opens up the world to exploration without even leaving home. With the Quest 2, exploration is easy and fun. If you’re thinking of trying it out, for yourself or a gift for someone young or old or in between, there’s never been a better time or a better and more affordable device than the Meta Quest 2.

[Edit] [Addition] I recently got new glasses, and while it comes with a spacer for glasses, I was using it without glasses because since I had cataract surgery and I thought my vision was good enough without wearing glasses. Although my distance correction was minimal, nearly the smallest size available, I got a great Black Friday deal on prescription lenses that snap right on to the regular lenses. This turned out to be one of the best accessories I've bought for my Quest 2. I highly recommend getting these, as long as your distance correction is a negative number. I hadn't realized how much I was settling for by not wearing my glasses because I found it uncomfortable. Now my vision is really crisp, and if someone else wants to try my headset, the lenses snap right off so they don't have to look through my prescription. I'm still enjoying my headset nearly every day. It's even got Amazon Prime Video available to watch on a big screen, which is a favorite of mine as I'm a Prime member.

review_title: Great out of the box - even better if you program it
review_text:
I bought this with Cherry Brown switches to replace a cheap bluetooth keyboard that I use to work from a remote location. I also have Vortex Pok3r and Filco TKL mechanical keyboards.

The build quality of the keyboard is good, but not quite as solid as my other mechanical keyboards. On the plus side it's lighter. The key action is nice and smooth, so it's very pleasant to type on. Keycaps seem high quality.

Out of the box I hated the fact that you have to type the modifier key to get tilde or backslash. These are pretty important keys for programming. However, this keyboard uses the open source QMK firmware, and it's easily programmable. I started with the web-based configurator and solved that problem quickly. But you can also program the firmware in C which opens up all sorts of possibilities (like static and dynamic macros, programming more layers, etc.). With full programmatic flexibility you can do pretty much anything you want in terms of customization.

I'd recommend this keyboard if you're willing to live with the default settings or are willing to take the effort to customize.

review_title: Great keyboard, of course depending on switches, but ...
review_text:
I think I finally found a keyboard, I'm happy to use in day in day out life. The Alt is great. I've bought it with Halo True switches but have to say they aren't my favorite. They are incredibly heavy right after the tactile bump, and I've started skipping characters due to this while typing fast. I switched them out for Halo Clear and I'm mostly happy now.

Since I need to have three workplaces, I bought one now and have two more on order from Drop. So far I'll stick with Halo Clear, but might test Cherry MX Silent Red in one of them.

Pros:

- The keyboard is sufficiently compact width wise, so that the mouse/trackpack isn't too far off the right side as to be uncomfortable. I find even TKL keyboards suboptimal in this regard, that's why I have the Alt, not the Ctrl.

- The selection options for switches could be a bit better. I'd love to have the OEM option for Silent Reds or some others. But okay, it's a small market, so difficult for manufacturers to offer "everything".

- The keycaps are high quality and just "feel good".

- The build quality is high. Aluminum top plate could use one or two studs in the middle to make it even more rigid.

- Hotswappable switches are a great idea. I love having them. As said above, I already switched from True to Clear. Was easy and done in about 15 minutes or so, including pulling the keycaps.

- Typing sound with Halo True and Clear switches is completely tolerable. Not very quiet, but also not very loud and from a noise/frequency perspective also not annoying. I'm pretty happy with it. Especially after I lubed the space bar stabilizer and placed some Gaffers tape underneath the stabilizers. Will probably do the other stabilizers as well since there is a slight amount of "ping" remaining.

Cons:

- I wish it had a function key row above the main block, preferably with a slight distance to the main block. The keyboard is fairly wide, but not deep, it would have added a significant functionality improvement to have these extra keys and not having to deal with pressing Fn all the time. Since the keyboard is heavy and bulky enough to not be considered portable, I'd really love to see this.

- I wish they the key caps were better visible without backlight, but okay, they have backlight and with it on full power whenever the keyboard wakes up from sleep, visibility is okay.

- There is a certain amount of pinging when typing fast. I haven't lubed all stabilizers yet, only the space bar, so I'm not sure I can get completely rid of it. We'll have to see, but just doing the space bar has made it sound significantly better. Space bar is now just a simple "thud", very satisfying, but took additional work.

Overall I'm very happy with this keyboard, I'm using it many hours per day and it'll only get more once I get the other ones for all locations. So, I can definitely recommend it for people looking for a flexible mechanical keyboard that is good for typing.

review_title: I tried to like this keyboard.
review_text:
I bought a refurb.

That being said...
-the iCUE software that is associated with programming the keyboard failed to recognize the keyboard about 80% of the time. The keyboard functioned without it, but the macros did not.
-The replaceable keycaps it came with for gaming are textured on the surface to find them easier, but they also have ridges that got annoying on the outer edges of the key groupings. (The top of W, left of A, bottom of S, right of D)
-The responsiveness of the speed keys was pretty wild, sometimes the weight of my fingers would activate a key, and without the click of actuation, I felt like it was the keyboards problem until I adjusted my posture.

-The wrist rest is a hard plastic material, no padding. It's also a rubbery texture, so if you have a shedding animal, or drop crumbs, you'll find it there.

All in all, I spent the 2-3 weeks I had this keyboard troubleshooting. Some of the forums I read explained the keyboard requires -specifically- USB 2. I don't have a USB 2 port on my computer unless it's a passthrough.

If your iCUE software doesn't recognize the keyboard, you can try changing the polling rate (within the software - this never worked for me, but it did for some).

If that fails, hold the escape key on the keyboard, unplug it, wait for 10 seconds, plug it back in, release the escape key. That does a firmware reset or something...

After playing Batman: Vengeance, it was an exhilarating change to have a protagonist who could fall off the side of a building and survive. My first impressions were: freedom!

But freedom comes at a price. Superman: Shadow of Apokolips is the first of its kind to allow you to play Superman with all of his abilities and in a fully rendered three-dimensional environment, but there are clipping errors and strange forced perspectives that ultimately dampen the game's enjoyment.

The plot is a loosely connected series of events involving the extra dimensional arch villain, Apokolips. Through his minion, Canto, he sets up a series of military-style attacks with "Apokoliptian technology" that he provides to Lex Luthor. Lex eventually sets a series of super villains free from Stryker Prison, including Livewire, Parasite, and Metallo. Or just Metallo's head in this case.

Lex is provided with a cadre of Interbots, strange goggle-eyed guys in masks. But don't worry, they're robots, so Superman can punch them without any gore. I was willing to accept the old G.I. Joe chestnut (i.e., "we have powerful guns, but let's run up to the bad guys and smash them in the face with our rifle butts!").

Punching Interbots is decidedly unsatisfying. Killing Interbots can be amusing at first. Setting them on fire with heat vision causes them to run around, arms flailing. They will sometimes run away, screaming in mechanical voices "This unit is compromised" or something like that. And yet, there's no feeling of Superman's awesome strength. When he hits Interbots, I want to see them go through walls, not just bounce around like rag dolls.

And there are so MANY of them. Superman fights Interbots, Interbot tanks, Interbot missle launchers, Interbot troop transports, Interbot gun emplacements, Interbots with jet packs, and Interbot helicopters. I don't ever recall seeing this many Interbots in the Superman cartoon.

Because of the sheer number of opponents, certain tactics are encouraged over others. Superman has a wide variety of abilities, including his x-ray vision, heat vision, super breath, super speed, flight, and super strength. But his best ability is an area attack slam that drops him at high speed onto the ground, knocking back and destroying everything in sight. This ability was more useful than punching Interbots. So suddenly, Superman becomes a living torpedo. Not necessarily a bad thing, but hardly representative of the Superman cartoon.

The game looks exactly like the movie, rendered in cell-shaded animation. All the voices actors are present, including Lori Petty as Livewire and Malcom McDowell as Metallo. But even those villains aren't the type who can go punch for punch with Superman.

Of all of the villains, only Livewire can fly. Superman slowly regenerates his damage and his super abilities. This means that if he is significantly harmed, you can just fly him away to a safe place and heal there. When fighting Metallo, I did this several times, while Metallo patiently waited down on the ground.

But I don't want to put the game down entirely. The game's plot is entertaining and even has a few twists. When the villains do show up, they are fully realized. I had a difficult time beating Livewire so I had plenty of opportunities to hear her wax poetic about electricity. I can't stand Lori Petty (except for her role in Tank Girl), but she really does act her heart out mocking Superman. Metallo does the same thing. There's a lot of entertainment value in just listening to them mock Superman. Superman returns the favor by talking to himself. Over and over and over. It gets annoying.

In terms of gameplay, there are a few high points. Superman must achieve the random feat of strength - plugging a damn, struggling through a wind tunnel. The game represents these challenges by requiring the player to tap a button repeatedly. Sadly, that mechanic isn't used enough.

The parts of the game that were most challenging (and sometimes frustrating) are the timed events. In essence, Superman must run an obstacle course before time runs out. If he fails...the screen goes white.

OH NO, SUPERMAN MUST BE DEAD!

Ahem. Given that Superman is near immortal, it's difficult to comprehend losing the game because, say, he didn't successful stave off a wind tunnel. So what? Superman would probably end up destroying the fan behind him without a scratch on him. Batman's mortality is precisely what raises the stakes - in Superman, it's hard to feel a sense of urgency for a man of steel.

At one point, Lex releases Metallo and encourages him to go after Superman. But Metallo, a cyborg, was originally created by Lex Luthor and ultimately betrayed by him by removing Metallo's head from his body. The first order of business for Metallo is to go after Lex.

The best part of the game is when Metallo shows up at Lex's office.

LEX: "Hello, Metallo. I was expecting to you."
METALLO: "Good, now stand right still while I remove YOUR head from YOUR body."
LEX: "Mercy?"

Lex nods towards Mercy, his female bodyguard who is carrying a large machinegun.

METALLO: "Not even if you beg."
LEX: "No you idiot, I mean her, behind you."
METALLO: "Do you seriously think I'm going to fall for-"

And that's when Mercy cuts loose with her machinegun, inflicting absolutely no damage whatsoever to Metallo. Unfortunately, Superman steps in at that point. It's telling that the best part of the game is a cut scene.

Overall, Superman: Shadow of Apokolips is an excellent realization of everyone's favorite superhero. Unfortunately, the game developers had difficulty providing challenges for the man of steel.

review_title: TINY TINA IS BACK AND SHE IS AS CRAZY AS EVER WITH HER BAD SELF!
review_text:
The more grown up Tiny Tina has lost some of her wild and crazy edge. Tiny Tina was at her Zenith in Boderlands 2 with all her talk of Bidonk- bidonks and explosives everywhere. In Borderlands 2 Tiny Tina was certifiably insane make no doubt about it. In Dragon's Keep Tiny Tina was stock raving barking mad and that is when she was at her very best. Every word she uttered was pure comic genius.

Somehow in Tiny Tina's Wonderlands she comes off as more muzzled and restrained which takes away from the silly over the top Cruella DeVille (animated version) type craziness she exuded. It is almost as if being a more mature woman has tempered and tamed Tina Tiny which was a bit depressing for me. Tiny Tina's hall mark was she was so over the top that it exceeded any definition of insanity. The voice actor for Tiny Tina in this instance should have been told to go as far over the top as you could because their was no upper limit in this role.

Technically the game play is rock solid. The frame rate is good on Xbox and PS4 pro systems. The explosions and colors are lovely. The in game loot is pure garbage. The Marcus, Doctor Ned and Ammo machines all serve nothing but garbage green and white level weapons. There is rarely a gold or even purple level weapon to buy or find while out in the world. Most of the in game guns are pretty lame. However having said all that the story is interesting and it is FUN!

The social justice warrior crowd have infested this game with they them fictional gender pronouns so I take a star off for that. The they them pronouns don't ruin the game play. The game does its best to emasculate strong white male characters like Brick. So there is a bit of SJW indoctrination not so subtly woven into the games DNA. Again the SJW element is there but again it does not really adversely impact game play. The fact that I bring all this up means my review will be censored or rejected.

This is a good game just not great. Tiny Tina's humor factor is on the ebb if this game is any indication. I brought this game and I am glad I did. I just wish it did not try to preach to me about subjects I don't think should be part of a video game. When I play video games all I am looking to do is have a spot of fun not be educated in the new socially correct political think!

review_title: MY GURL IS BACK! TINY TINA IS BACK AND CRAZIER THAN EVER! AND I AM LOVING IT!
review_text:
The best DLC in Borderlands history in my humble opinion was Tiny Tina and Dragon's Keep DLC in Borderlands 2. I was not as happy with Tiny Tina in Borderlands 3 because she had lost her sick twisted edge. Tiny Tina was played as more mature and responsible in Borderlands 3 which to me made her painfully forgettable. I almost didn't buy Tiny Tina's Wonderlands because in Borderlands 3 Tiny Tina had grown up to be a crashing uninteresting uninspired by the numbers adult bore.

Yet when I saw Tina Tina looking at me from the box art, I spied a hint of her old stone cold crazy in the way she was drawn. I was wondering had the writers seen the light and made my Tiny Tina stock raving mad again. What I loved about Tiny Tina was not her age per-se. I loved that the original Tiny Tina seemed to think she was absolutely normal while in fact she was bonkers. I loved how she showed no respect for any human conventions. Hell she called Brick Gurl in one instance! In Borderlands 3 she lost that totally insane vibe she had captured and perfected in Borderlands 2.

So I got Tiny Tina's Wonderlands because, I wanted to see if my crazy as heck Tina was back. Well Tina is still a little more bland than she was in Borderlands 2 Dragon Keep DLC but she is much more energetic and nutz in Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. I know what happened. The haters said Tiny Tina a white character was modeled too closely to black human female attributes citing cultural appropriation to which I say horse feathers!

Tiny Tina is a product of awesome imagination that resulted from a blend of different forms of crazy over the top Creulla DeVille, Norma Desmond and Auntie Mame inputs. Yes there is a black influence but it exists among many other influences that made Tiny Tina insane.

Well about the game play. It is solid. I have been playing for well over 50 hours on PS4 Pro without issue. No screen tearing. No crashes. No video issues or artifacts. No frame rate issues. The start is a bit long before the action starts heating up. This is not DLC repackaged as main game content but this is short for a Borderlands franchise spin off game. Now this is NOT strictly a Borderlands Game as it occurs inside the warped mind of Tiny Tina using a sort of Dungeons and Dragon game format.

You are immersed in the game and from there you must follow the path Tina lays out and remember Tiny Tina is straight up stone cold NutZ! The graphics are great if you love every color in the rainbow and then some. The game has some political correctness in it allowing you to choose weird They\Them\Theirs Pronouns outside of the purely normal binary he\him\his - she\her\hers. Funny thing weird pronouns are in keeping with Borderlands sexually fluid lore.

Pandora was a crazy house. Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is a fun game even with Tiny Tina on more of a leash than I like. Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is a fun romp. Tiny Tina's Wonderlands game play uses many of the mechanics and tropes found in Borderlands but it has a few new twists. You can cast spells. Fight Dragons and orks. Shields and med packs have been rebranded but function as expected. Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is more linear than the more open world Borderlands series. The Tiny Tina's Wonderlands menu system is still a hot mess.

I love Tiny Tina's Wonderlands because even watered down Tiny Tina remains just crazy enough for me to enjoy my time spent with her in game. Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is not the over the top fun that Tiny Tina in Dragons Keep was but Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is like returning home after growing up. Yeah its different but it is still home and Tiny Tina while subdued is still mad as a hatter!

review_title: A Gamble on a 3rd Party Controller paid off!
review_text:
I was not too sure about getting this controller, sometimes when i see a piece of electronic accessory that's much cheaper than the competition, i get worried. So i gambled a bit on buying this controller... And have to say, don't regret it one bit!

Controller is comfortable in hands, buttons click nicely , and both buttons and joysticks have a good feel. The controller actually felt heavier at first glance then what i expected- but, for me, that's a good thing. The placement of the Home and + / - buttons are a little too close together, however, i wish they were more tactile and further apart. Oh, and Yes, this controller comes with RUMBLE.

For those of you who want to know, the instructions for pairing is pretty straightforward. You press the Home button for 3 seconds, and wait for the LED lights to flash. Then hold the L and R triggers for about 3 seconds, and it should pair with the switch without a hitch. You do need to be in the Controller Configuration screen on the Switch to make this work, though. Its a little awkward when you first do it wirelessly, but after a couple times it's really easy , and it works very well. Like a number of 3rd party controllers that I've seen, this controller will NOT wake up the Switch if you put it too sleep.

The only thing i can say that is a slight negative about this controller is (what i assume to be) a battery saving feature on this controller, which is annoying. If you don't use the controller for a few minutes, it disconnects and turns off by itself. Wish it would last longer!

Other then that, this is a great 3rd party controller. Haven't had any issues with it, pairing is fast (and easy when you get the hang of it), and feels good and comfortable in the hands. Oh, and it's about a 1/3rd the cost of Nintendo's Pro controller. ... What more could you ask for...?

I actually did enjoy the game. There were some good points, and some bad ones. I'll start with the bad.
1. It was glitchy. Your character may get stuck in some areas. Shutting the game down, and restarting usually fixes this, and you go back to your last save point.
2. Another issue I had, was that I lost all of my skill points that I built for my Vampires towards the middle-end of the game. I'm not quite sure if they were supposed to reset, but I had to build them up from scratch, which prevented my vampire's abilities from being so advanced. I was able to finish the game, though.
3. (Possible bad) I will advise you to read all the reading material in the menu option before playing the game or you will be lost. Just set aside some time, and read it. It's a lot of reading material, but I must say, it helped me become more involved in the game, and the characters when I knew their backstories, and certain terms that I would not have been familiar with while playing. If you do not like reading, then you may not enjoy this part. It was very time consuming.
4. While playing the game, there is a lot of long, unnecessary reading of unnecessary documents. I wish they had made those shorter if they did not help you progress in the game. I read everything to make sure I could solve any clues. Again, time consuming, but in a bad way.
5. Try to walk slowly through rooms, not run, or you may miss something. Take your time.
6. The graphics feel a bit outdated for a game in 2022. In the beginning it seemed fine, and then the characters seemed to look less polished as the game went on.
7. The endings could have explained more no matter which ending you ended up with. Some of the endings outright skipped revealing what happened to certain vampires, leaving you to assume. With all the reading to be done in this game, I expected to know what happened to all of the vampires that I had read so much about. I feel that was laziness on their part when it came to telling a proper ending.
8. I wear glasses, but I wish they made the font a bit larger for all the reading I had to do.
Now the good.
1. I liked the characters. All different, with different backstories.
2. The puzzles, and solving things were fun and challenging, but not impossibly hard.
3. I liked the different, unique abilities each vampire could use.
4. Despite the bugs, and lengthy reading, I still enjoyed playing the game. I would replay it.
5. I like that you can skip until you have a question to answer, because if you replay the game, or a scene, it can take a while with the dialogue.

Overall, it was satisfying enough if you are a patient person who likes to explore, and like decision based games, and playing multiple characters.

If I had a nickle for every time a game I loved was popular in Japan but not over here...it's the story of my gaming life.
