It's an okay game I guess. Graphics are above average and the gameplay is interesting but like just about any other Tom Clancy game it has an air of childishness about it. What it actually is is a very dumbed down RTS game designed to function well on the consoles, which is the real reason there is a voice command system. Beware though, more than a tiny bit of ambient noise can make it malfunction. The good thing is that using the voice command is optional. Most likely on the PC you won't want/need to use it.

So anyway, you can actually finish this game in as little as 3 turns but you can drag it out longer than that and you can play or replay as a different country but what you'll find is that no matter what country you play or what strategy you use the game is always the same. There are some annoyances like the WMD option that you get if you are losing the game but the thing is that once you use it then the other side gets the option too and there's really not much you can do but resign yourself to losing a lot of units. About the only remedies to this is to always attack on two fronts, never jumble up your forces in a small area, and don't try to overwhelm the enemy with sheer numbers. Keep plenty on reserve.

It's cool to be able to upgrade your weapons and armor and the upgrades do work very well, they aren't just for show. You can even change the camo patterns. This feature is, in my opinion, about the best the game has to offer. Enemy AI will at times pull some good tricks out of it's hat but for the most part it's a simple, go through the motions and you're done type of game. Typical of Tom Clancy games in that even on the hardest settings they are never very hard to complete, mostly I think because they were made for kids.

I guess as long as you don't go into this thing expecting large-scale,epic battles that require alot of planning and strategy then you'll be satisfied. I replaced this twice with aftermarket keys. I even added my own felt buffers in an effort to keep it from failing. It's just an awful design. The fact that aftermarket space bars even exist for this keyboard speaks volumes.

Not long after I got the keyboard it started doubling. It eventually got to the point it was unusable with the "N", "R" and "Esc" keys chattering so bad that some times as many at 5 or 6 strokes would register per press. Later the "N" key eventually stopped registering key presses at all.

The LEDs began failing in about 6 months. After 2 years many keys had completely lost at least one LED and the "W" key was totally burned out.

The switches. I don't get why "Cherry" switches are so popular. The Brown Cherry is supposed to be quiet. (Somebody in Cherry MX's marketing needs to look up what a brown cherry really is.) There are 3rd party keymods that are intended to quiet them down. But, when the key travel stops with the key striking a metal sounding board it's a futile effort. Even the Brown Cherry keys sound like you're typing with a jackhammer.

Flashy garbage. If Corsair spent the effort and money making a flashing light up logo on the actual functionality of this keyboard maybe it might not be such junk. The keys are wobbly, flimsy and frail. Typing this review on a keyboard from a competitor makes me realize how truly awful the K95 was.

I was fortunate in that I'd purchased an Asuron protection plan with this. It's on its way back now. Hopefully Asuron has a proper e-waste disposal program because the Corsair K95 was e-waste the day it was made. None of these failures can be attributed to it being an Amazon Warehouse Referb. The one I got appeared to be new and was probably just an open box return. Somebody else dodged a bullet when they returned it. review_title: An amazing tale of fun and...fun!
review_text:
Think Grandia. That's all I could imagine when I played it. The stories are nothing alike, just the character's innocence and excitement for their journey. For those who haven't been graced by Grandia, this a typical coming of age/adventure story that isn't directly involved in an ongoing war. There are wars going on in these games but your characters aren't fighting for any side. The exciting part is watching your characters grow as people and all the interaction with their excitement of seeing the world. On a separate note, try Grandia if end up loving this.

I will warn everyone that this is a dialogue adventure, so if you don't like story or enjoying your character's development you will be bored through 50% of the game. I must mention the dialogue is excellent written, not entirely intelligent banter but gets its point across perfectly. I'm not one for stupid Japanese humor (bitchy girls, emasculated boys, furry sidekicks), and this is very light on stupid jokes, taking a rather serious tone at times.

As for game play, you walk, talk, and fight. Luckily there are fun places to walk through to enjoy detail. Then talking, there's a lot. A nice feature is the NPC dialogue changes a lot so I actually talked to them repeatedly, which I never do. Then comes fighting. Sneak up behind your enemy for a preemptive strike to secure victory. Attack them directly or with spells/skills from your equipped materia... I mean quartz. Lots of combos and goodies to play with. Also, if you're beat up or attack enough, you build up your limit break... I mean special attack bar to release some cool attacks.

Im sure you get the picture. It is fun, that's not sarcasm up there.

I definitely suggest it! And I'm not going to say I have any more experience than you by saying "I've played most and am an expert". Sure both may be true... But it shouldn't affect your judgment. Let's just say after so many boring, tired, pointless, plotless, lifeless videogames this one surely will breathe life back into your love for RPGs. Because let's face it, sometimes its easy to forget why we loved them in the first place with all the trash we've played.

Try it, you won't be disappointed. Thanks for reading.

review_title: Tight graphics, decent gameplay, and annoying features
review_text:
The Good:
- Graphics are impressive with good lighting effects and nice scenery blur as speed ramps up. The cars look great, with realistic reflections.

- Races are fast paced and fun. There are a good variety in the type of races, from drag runs to point-2-point to circuit races.

- Car customization is just right. There are enough upgrades, both performance and visual, to spend hours pimping your ride. I love the interior customization, all the way down to trim/fabric colors, lighting, etc. Its really impressive that they modeled the original stock interior for all these cars!

The Bad:
- Maybe I'm in the minority, but I hate having to drive around to find races. This isn't GTA, I just want to race. It is a real pain having to track down the race you want, flash your brights, etc. Sure it may seem more realistic, but again this isn't GTA.

- The pedestrians are idiots and don't add anything to the gameplay.

- Music is so-so

- Car selection could be better.

- Car physics are completely unrealistic and get quite frustrating after a while.

- Online play is fun, but there is never a level playing field. You race with your POS starter car while the other guys have Aston Martins... real fair.

The Verdict:
If you must have a racing game to tie you over until the next Gran Turismo is released, this will do. Just don't expect much replay value.

review_title: A lot shorter than I expected
review_text:
You probably already know what this game is, but if not it's in short a puzzle game. There's no real "combat", mostly just following "clues" and putting objects together to try to solve puzzles.

First off, it runs well on Windows 7 64-bit systems. It had some weird graphical bugs on my ATI card, though restarting the game made them go away. I haven't tried it with a nVidia card yet. Graphics are good for what they try to be, cartoony and not overly realistic.

There's a lot of dialog and a lot of effort put into it. The worlds look nice and the world is small enough to generally be able to find things that you need. The puzzles were for the most part fun.

Some of the design seems a bit lazy. You go into the forest at one point and going back the same way you came seems to send you to a new location instead of where you were before. It's hard to explain, but was OK after I got used to it. The puzzles are bizarre at times and I still never figured out how you're supposed to know how to turn some of the dials. I mostly had to use luck and a little logic (though I'm positive not the way the developers intended) to trial and error my way through. I beat the game without a guide, but parts of it were highly tedious.

I was pretty shocked how short the game was. I was expecting to travel the entire island, but only ended up going to a handful of locations. The whole point is to stop some winds, get a boat, and sail off to the next game. After you get off the island, that's it. Go get the next chapter. Not that big a deal for me because I got the whole set on a 1 day sale, so all of them cost me less than half the price of one here, but if you're paying full price it's only a few hours of fun and really no replay value.

The second chapter is driving me nuts though. I may have to break down and try a guide. It seems more difficult in the randomness of how the puzzles need to be solved and more locations mean more load times while hunting around. Morgan is hot at least. ;)

review_title: Short Games but as a Collection, Decent.
review_text:
This is a pretty simplistic game by the standards of a StarCraft or WarCraft, or Supreme Commander, but that doesn't make it bad. It's quite a fun game. In an era of huge video card requirements and maps that are so big you'll lose track of your units, I appreciated the approach.

The only cons I can give it are weak AI and the lame practice of only putting 1 race campaign in the first game and leaving all the others to skirmish. That's right, you only get to play as the Space Marines. Come on, that's just lazy. They made a bit more effort in the single player on the expansion, but still really short change you on single player levels.

Dark Crusade is arguably the best of the bunch, but doesn't strictly have any single player levels. It's sort of like a game of Risk where you have to conquer the whole map. Most of the map is skirmish levels, but the home base for each race is more a standard set piece where you have to finish specific objectives to win. When taken as a package for the price, this package seems it's a pretty decent, though not terribly long, game. If you like playing the skirmish missions, you can get a lot of fun out of it.

review_title: This is my second mechanical keyboard by Durgod. It's not cheap, but for good reasons.
review_text:
As I wrote in the title of this review, this is my second mechanical keyboard by Durgod. My first one has the very same design and layout, but it's the non-backlit White key-caps model with the 'Clicky' Tactile Blue key switches, which are the NOISIEST Cherry MX keys you can find; at the time when these keyboards came out I wanted the old school classic 'clicky' sound when typing. But as the time went by it became irritating, which led me to begin considering a less noisy model. And of course, I came back to check Durgod's new models as since I purchased my first one, many new Cherry MX keys came out, each with a different color switches that represent specific features, along with the pros and cons which altogether is a matter of taste. And the reason I didn't look elsewhere is because the Durgod keyboards are built like a TANK! You will justify the high price you paid for the moment you hold their heavy keyboards in your hands. So you pay for a very good quality.

When I checked the available keyboards I first wanted a less noisy typing experience, but I still wanted to have enough feedback from the keys when typing. Then I saw that there is a standard backlit model with white backlit light, and a RGB model that really got my attention, as you can basically change the backlit color to whatever color you like, and even to save and load color presets to your liking.

The RGB backlit model comes in black key-caps while the surrounding frame of the keyboard is a mixture of black with a slight of red which I didn’t see in the pictures – I expected a pure black color, but it looks good anyway. The Cherry MX switches options for this RGB model are Black, Blue and Brown. From all the three the Brown keys are the most popular amongst gamers as far as I read and watched online, as they're not too noisy, but still gives the user the right tactile feedback when pressing on them.

Attached to this review a bunch of pictures I took of my old Durgod keyboard (white) and the current RGB backlit model for visual comparison.

As you can see, both keyboards look alike and are in the same measurements and height. But the backlit model has shorter key-caps which makes the bottom of the keys to look more ‘exposed’. While some users would prefer longer key-caps, the reason these are shorter is in order to reveal the light that comes from below the key-caps, which surrounds each key with a stroke of light. If the key-caps were longer then less light would have shine around them.

Packaging thoughts:
Amazon sure knows how to pack expensive products. Thanks Amazon!

Box content:
- USB Type-C to Type-C cable
- USB Type-C to Type-A cable
- Key-caps lifter to take the key-caps off for cleaning or for replacing
- Keyboard plastic protecting cover when not in use (highly recommend to keep dust away!)
- Booklet
- Cable management scotch
- Coaster(?) :)

Typing thoughts:
Honestly, I'm typing this review with this keyboard and it both feels great and sounds great! I even feel that I'm typing with less effort, that the keyboard gives me just the right tactile feedback, and the sound of typing isn’t irritating to the ears since it’s only Tactile and not ‘Clicky Tictle’ like the Blue switches. I just love this keyboard and very pleased that I picked this model!

Looking thoughts:
Having a keyboard with white backlit light is great. But having RGB backlit light is even better! And the reason is because you can change the light color to your liking. I have a laptop with a white backlit keyboard and found that the white light is less convenient to the eyes when working in the dark. With this keyboard however I changed the light color to orange/yellowish, which feels much more pleasant to the eyes in my opinion. There’s a preset of a single backlit color, and you can press Fn+Pause and see all the available colors to pick from. I don’t need anything fancy with multiple colors. Just having the option to select a color hue to my taste worth everything.

Bottom line:
I highly recommend this keyboard to anyone. But if you're struggling to decide which Cherry MX switches to pick, I highly recommend you to watch the "Cherry MX Switch Comparison" by 'KeyMouse' on YouTube. The guy made a very informative video showing the differences of all the Cherry MX key switches, giving you an idea of how they both behave and sound. Keep in mind thought that not all key switches are available for the backlit models. So I think that the Brown switches are the best choice between tactile feel and not-noisy typing experience.

CRYPTIC PASSAGE was the long-awaited, and apparently the final, add-on to what I consider the most enjoyable PC game of all time: BLOOD. Having played the living $%#! out of the original game and the superb PLASMA PAK add-ons, I was very excited to get my paws on this. Ten new levels of hemoglobin-drenched mayhem (plus a hidden level) were calling my name, and my name was Caleb!

Unfortunately, it seems that CRYPTIC PASSAGE was rushed prematurely to the marketplace. It is not a very well-designed game at all, which is to say that the game itself is fine, but the glitches and bugs in the system conspired to make it virtually unplayable.

The original BLOOD had an extremely smooth, flowing play and graphics which were remarkbly high-resolution for their day (the mid-90s). Ditto the PLASMA PAK. CRYPTIC PASSAGE, on the other hand, was incredibly choppy, with stuttering, glitch-ridden movement and cruddy graphics quality that made everything look dull and rather coarse-textured in appearance. The latter is only annoying, but the former made it very hard to actually play the game. After extensively tinkering with the Mo'Slo program speed in DOS, I was able, with the help of an IT friend, get the game to play half-decently, but I was never able to get it play RIGHT. Which was very frustrating, because as far as the screens went, CRYPTIC was very well done.

Vengeful antihero Caleb, still apparently on a rampage even after settling accounts with treacherous Tchernobog the God, starts in a boatyard and faces the usual assortment of dynamite-hurling monks and brain-hungry zombies, shooting his way through an old opera house, a gothic library, a monastery, a riverboat, and others, until he ends up in a huge castle at the end. The game's climax is lame, with Caleb merely discovering some hidden scrolls rather than tackling a Big Bad God or 200 monks and monsters, but the buildup is satisfying. There are no new weapons or beasties, but the change of venue and the ample supply of people and creatures to set ablaze with the flare gun or explode with the napalm cannon were enough to satisfy the homicidal maniac in me. (I did find the hidden level very disappointing as well, it was merely a swamp filled with fish-monsters who I promptly sent packing to Mrs. Paul.)

I would never dog BLOOD, I think it is just the best first-person shooter ever, but my experience with CRYPTIC was a downer. Like all BLOOD games, it won't run on anything more advanced than Windows 98, and it won't run by itself, either. Other gamers may have had a more positive experience, and if they know how to make the game run more smoothly, I'd appreciciate a flare in my direction.

UPDATE TO REVIEW - 7/6/12

Using something called the DOSBox, which I downloaded from GOG.com, I am now able to play this game as it was intended. The graphics looks good, the play is extremely smooth (about 95% of the original), and the music, and I can now hear the musical score, which is amazing - evocative, terrifying, and beautiful. I still think the game has some lame levels and lacks a proper climax, but it is so much improved by playing it via the DOSbox as to almost represent a new game. So I'd amend my review to four starts and strongly advise BLOOD players to do as I have done and get the box!

review_title: Perfect grips and great case, even though it is not as depicted
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:7b9bc82e5eef6933682f45b45a6bec3d]] This video highlights the functionality of the grips, the mini-touch pen, and the missing case flap. Below is my review of this item, you can also find my images with notes on here.

Case:
The case is a nice hard case with soft felt inside and elastic straps the secure the vita inside so it doesn't fly out when you open it. The case comes with a detachable wrist strap of its own. The outside of the case is a soft unbranded matte leather or pleather. I like this because it keeps the item inside discrete. However I was very disappointed to find that it does not have the inner flap as shown on the website. I think this inner flap would increase the overall functionality of the case because it could protect the screen from hard items in the mesh side of the case. I am going to contact amazon and see if they can replace just the case itself so it is the right one. I will post the results of that request here when I have them. (update 7/25/12: I never got around to asking for a swap out and am realizing today that it doesn't bother me anymore. to be honest even the little game boxes and strap things don't seem to scratch the vita so it's fine as is. i do also have a screen protector on my vita as i do with all my devices.) All in all I am happy with the case and give it 4 out of 5 stars because it isn't as shown and I really wanted that protective flap that could hold game cards as was shown on the site when I purchased. I give this item 4 out of 5 because it really should have the middle flap shown.

Mini-Touch Pen:
It's a nice little pen that works well and is very responsive on the screen. Now all I need is a painting app for the vita. It also works well on my phone so that is a plus. I threw out the little pin that came in the end of it because it only works in the headphone jack and makes it impossible to use headphones at the same time. Instead I just used the loop it is on in one of the vita's wrist strap loops and it works well there. I give this item 5 out of 5 for the pen.

Grips:
For some reason I imagined these to be silicone grips or at least a soft touch grip set. They are not. The grips are hard plastic only. They have little notches in them to allow you to keep wrist straps etc. attached to the vita while in the grips. As the video shows they slip onto the vita and snap in fairly gently. I picked this kit primarily because I like the way this grip appeared in function on the pictures on amazon and I have not been disappointed here. I am not worried at all about slipping the vita in and out of grips to alternate between them and the case. The actual click spots on the grips are very small, and do not overlap the vita very far, they also do not interfere with the button actions of any buttons at all. The grips feel wonderful in my hand; they are pretty much the perfect size for me a 5'-6" female. I will probably not play the vita without them from now on. I give these 5 out of 5.

Neck-strap:
The next strap is a nice nylon or similar soft fabric and comes with a clip on the end so you can detach the vita from the strap if need be, I have noted this on my photos. It is pretty comfortable around the neck but a bit short for me and where I like my playing distance to be. It's about 4" short for my taste, I like to hold be able to rest my hands in my lap while playing. I give this one 4 out of 5 because it should be a touch longer.

Wrist strap:
The wrist strap is a very soft rayon type fabric; it is not exactly the same as the neck strap but is very comfortable. It has a little piece on it that will shrink down to close on your wrist as every good wrist strap should have. No detachable clip though, which I am also okay with. The downer is that the plastic attachment and tightener pieces are hard plastic and only fit in the case one way, on top of the vita. I don't like this and will probably take the strap on and off when I use it. The fastener piece will fit attached in the case if you put it right over one of the two speakers or over the buttons... if I do leave it on I'll probably do it over the speakers but am a little worried it might scratch the vita. I give these 4 out of 5 stars since the attachment could have been a softer less sharp design.

Game case:
These are throwaways to me, I mean I might use them but then again I probably won't. They are slightly larger than a game itself and to me when I have that many games that I need them I'll just by the long Sony case that holds games and memory sticks because I think that one will be harder to loose. These are still small enough to disappear. I was really counting on the inner flap to put my extra games in until I have a large collection that justified the long Sony game case. However since my case didn't come with that flap I'll probably just get the long case when I buy a second game, right now I only have one game. I rate these 2 out of 5 stars since it would be better for helping you keep track of games if they were one case that held three games or an a flap attached to the case.

Screen protector and cleaner, etc.:
The screen protector, cloth, and soft card are par for the course when it comes to screen protectors. I haven't used them yet because I already have a Sony brand protector on there and it is in good shape still. One thing I can say is it would be nice to see other companies make the screen protectors with a screen finding template like the Sony one has. When my screen needs a new protector I will use this one and update the review here. As far as the cleaner goes, I don't see myself using it. I might test it out on a monitor or something at some point and will update this if I do.

Charger & USB cable:
The converter brick part is nice because it puts the business end all at one side. The downside to it is that if you plug it into a standard wall outlet it will either block the plug below or it will block the ground (third plug) above it. I haven't tried it in a power strip, but I imagine it will be the same. The USB cable is solid feeling, more so than the one that came with the vita, when you plug it into the vita. The only other downside is that USB cable is a standard 4' length or so, so this means your charging distance would be shorter than if you used the Sony charging brick with two cords. . I rate the power brick 2 out of 5 stars and the USB cable 5 out of 5 stars.

Headphones:
The headphones are cheap but usable in a backup situation. There is no real bass reproduction in them and so everything sounds like tweeter, even deep bass music like jungle, dub, hip-hop, or blues. They are also really big feeling in the ears. I will hang onto them because it is always nice to have an extra pair around just-in-case you lose or break your good set and need to go for a while. I would not however buy these as your main set of headphones as they are uncomfortable and sound is terrible. I rate them 2 out of 5 stars.

Bottom line:
I bought this item because I was looking for both a set of grips that were not oversized and a nice solid case and I found them with this pack. I give the item 4 out of 5 stars overall because a few of the items were not as depicted on the site. For me the case and grips are solid enough with a great price point that I would recommend this pack to anyone, I would also buy it again for the grips alone.

review_title: A Game That Lives Up To The Hype
review_text:
DUKE NUKEM FOREVER is a now-infamous video game that some waited 15 years to play, and this alone is cause for many of the game's bad reviews. I, however, was only six years old when Duke Nukem 3D came out and, even though I played the game all throughout my childhood years (and still love it), I never really waited for a sequel and eventually forgot about it until a year or two ago. Then the game last year and no one seemed to like it and some of the reviews told of things that I knew I wouldn't like, and that was almost depressing.

But I got the game anyway and I do NOT regret it.

DNF lives up to my expectations as someone who has played all the Duke Nukem games and knows what it is that makes Duke DUKE. It is truly a worthy successor to DN3D: lots of action, lots of aliens, and more hilarious one-liners from Duke. The story is fun, too.

The only downsides are these:
1) No jet-pack.
2) Limited range of level exploration
3) Very limited weapons inventory*
4) It is sometime unclear what you're supposed to do.

*The weapon inventory has received a ton of criticism (you get two gun slots standard), but I think it can be defended as such: it ads a level of difficulty that gamers should appreciate (unless you just don't like a challenge). Also, you really should be playing the game on PC (it's the superior and intended version), which gives the option of holding four guns instead of two. The four-gun system works well, as it lets you have three of your favorite guns and a fourth slot for whatever special weapon the level demands, or just four guns you like best and screw the rest. I like it.

As for the packaging of the BALLS OF STEEL EDITION and the bonus materials: it's good stuff. It all seems smaller than you might expect, but the overall deal creates a sense of appreciation for the fans on the creator's behalf. You can tell they want to make up for the insane wait and they do a great job. The bust is detailed and awesome, the 100 page book is a nice companion piece to the game (and the game's unlockable bonus material), the comic book is great for a laugh, the sticker will look awesome on your laptop or pc, the paper craft is an unusual but neat addition; the cards are small but nice and the accompanying poker chips and dice are very cool.

And finally: all this for under $25. INSANE. You get a modern game with all that extra stuff for less than the price of the cheapest modern games for 360 and PS3. It really is an unbeatable deal that any fan of Duke can appreciate. I'd give it a TEN STAR rating if I could, just for all the fun and laughs I had playing this excellent game.

review_title: Good strategy game with a steep learning curve.
review_text:
This is a very good game. It's a turn based strategy/rpg tactical game. Earth has "allied" itself with aliens from another world. They are secretly bad guys doing a hostile takeover from within. A resistance was formed to fight back. You are the leader of that resistance. It's a simple, but great story. The game is very similar to Final Fantasy Tactics with a big overall story and various battles along the way to advance through it. In this game though, there are more variables. It's true a race against time to stop the aliens from finished a game ending project. Think of it as a clock advancing to 12 midnight, which is doom. Each time you thwart a major alien event, the clock moves back. You can approach the war the way you want to, but you can't just sit back and farm. There's a lot to like about this game, but it has it's flaws. Let's start with the pros.

Pros:

This game has excellent customization and rpg elements. You can customize and change just about everything about your troops. Your troops get better as they gain experience and can specialize in certain classes, like Sharpsooters or Rangers. It really ended up getting me very attached to them. There's also building, research and development within your flying base, which reminds me of the SHIELD Helicarrier from Captain America. There are various missions you must perform affecting the main story, but also hot spots that crop up that you can address or ignore. Lot's of great stuff. I also noticed that the game changes every time you start a new one. The battles are never the same. That makes replay value off the charts. The battles themselves are a lot fun. There's a ton of strategy involved. You absolutely cannot just charge in gung ho and expect to win. No way. You must plan and pay attention to everything.

Cons:

Of course, the game is not perfect. Don't be fooled by the "Rookie" mode on the difficulty settings. Uh, no. This game does have four modes, but they should be named Hard, Harder, Super Hard, and Insane. This game is punishing at times. In the overall scope of the campaign, a few wrong choices will sink your game and hand victory to the aliens. I've had to restart it twice already. It's also very unforgiving for your troops. You can spend hours building up your elite troops, only to see them die from one or two shots from a rank and file alien. If they get wounded, they will be unavailable to you for days even weeks at a time. That leaves you with scrubs to fight even harder missions. It's tough going. I've angrily closed the game down many times after losing my best troops during a battle. My advice to you is to save often. Another thing that drives me crazy is the slow load times for this game. It is the slowest loading game I have seen on the PS4. Skyrim loads way faster. I don't get why. This game is not graphics intensive, by any means. Think PS3 level graphics. It also gets choppy for cut scenes. Why? How? It also takes forever to load saved games. That's poor game programming to me. Even the battles progress slowly at times for no reason. Not graphics slow do down, but time waiting for the aliens to make their moves. Add to that the annoying ship captain who always chimes in over and over to tell you things you already know. It wouldn't be so annoying if the game didn't pause while he's yammering away. Another thing that drives me absolutely nuts, is the way the game is constantly throwing things at you. In the campaign map, you can't seem to do anything without an event popping up in multiple places with that annoying captain bothering you with things. Sometimes all you want to do is get some supplies, but sometimes endless events interrupt you. "Commander, we have Advent attacking a settlement", "Commander, the aliens are advancing their Avatar project, we must....", "Commander we must make contact with other resistant forces.....", "Commander this...Commander that". God, SHUT UP and let me get my supplies for crying out loud. It's only three days. Leave me ALONE!!!! It's constant sometimes and annoying. There have been times I just hit the ignore button out of frustration.

Overall though, it's a good game with a steep learning curve. I noticed that after restarting the game twice, the fun level increased exponentially. If you learn from your mistakes, you will get better and appreciate the good that this game has to offer. My advice is to stick with it. If you like strategy and have some patience, you will like this game. I give it a thumbs up.

I was one of those that thought the graphics engine was actually beautiful to look at, however, it could have used more optimization to get it to run faster. I finished both games just fine, but there were many times my framerates would fall below 20 fps, and it didn't matter how I tweaked the graphics settings. So if you buy this game, be prepared. You may have trouble with framerates no matter what you do. But even then, I think it's a great game to have.

review_title: Possibly the Pinacle of the Franchise
review_text:
I have to admit that I never played Vesperia on the Xbox 360. I'm a huge Jrpg fan and an equally large fan of the Tales of series in general so missing out on what many consider to be the best game in the franchise was kind of a stain on my record. Thankfully the PS4 remaster came around right as I decided to play through the entire franchise (goodbye to so many hours of my life) so I eagerly scooped it up on release and plugged it in to see if it's as good as I hear. Thankfully I can report that not only is it better than I hoped, but it has also probably dethroned Symphonia as my favorite Tales of title. Let's discuss.

Graphics: Vesperia is beautiful. It's as simple as that. If you like the anime aesthetic and have a 4k TV you should be pleasantly surprised by how good this game looks. The colors pop off the screen in a way that I don't think an anime type game has before. I was curious so I picked up a 360 version of the game and tried it out. The old version itself looks great for a game released in 2008, but the remaster really stands out to me for both its art style and dedication to a bright vibrant palette. Honestly it looks better than Berseria (the most recent game in the franchise). The anime cut scenes are somewhat a weak point, with slow frame rates and older quality animation, but they are by no means bad and considering it's a game from 2008, I'll give it a pass. There are a few areas with some frame dropping issues but this seems to be getting patched out and the experience in general is a very smooth 60fps.

Gameplay: Gameplay, as usual, is the most important part of the game to me and realistically this is where Vesperia falls a little behind the newer games in the franchise. It's a flat out button masher most of the time. Of course you can mix in technical abilities, burst artes, and spell casting, but the lack natural 3D movement and extra combat gimmicks (like the armitization system in Zesteria) make it a tad dated. Its combat more resembles Symphonia than Xillia and is relatively easy to understand and execute. The real strategy comes in forming a well balanced party and learning which artes to use at which times.

Story: without getting into too many spoilers, the story of Vesperia follows Yuri and Estelle as they set out on a journey to find mutual friend Flynn. From there, their tale will take them far and wide and eventually lead them to building a strong cast of friends with various personalities and motivations. The cast is really good in this game and the definitive edition even comes complete with content that was removed from the US release on 360 as well as mountain of extra skits, outfits and scenes. The only real weak point for me was Patty and her story, which was kind of byzantine and took me a while to fully understand (she was a cut character from the original release). The skits in this game are solid and remind me of Symphonia's skits which I always felt were more relevant and interesting than Berseria's endless diatribes on pirate lifestyle choices. As a note the new skits added in the definitive version have a different voice actor for Yuri than in the original. You do notice it from time to time, but the voices are close enough and for me personally it wasn't a big deal. The Japanese audio is also present for the dub purists among us The story all in all is solid and presents moral quandaries and ethically challenging moments that the franchise would eschew until Berseria released nearly a decade later (while I love Xillia 1 and 2, they don't come close to this story cohesion wise). The music is really solid jrpg fare. Not stand out, but by no means bad.

Conclusion: Vesperia is great. It's solid in story, has beautiful 4k graphics that give Persona 5 a run for its money, and the gameplay, while not as complex as future titles, is solid and a decent amount of fun. Realistically if you are a fan of anime, jrpgs, or looking to break into the genre, this game is a great investment. I played for about 65 hours and enjoyed every bit of it. Definitely give it a go. To me it was worth new game price and has been better the 90% of the AAA market over the last year (shoutout to Bandai Namco for releasing a finished non buggy game even if it is a remaster).

Unlike many Wii peripherals, both the game play and fun-factor are improved by having a gun for first person shooters. This, however, is not the gun to get.

review_title: I'm slowly catching up on VG's so bare with me
review_text:
For years now i've loved playing the first GTA. I hadnt played it for a while and I ended up playing it again recently for the hell of it. The only other GTA game i'd ever played was a demo to GTA London that didnt impress me... well, thanks to someone telling me you can now download this game for free, i figured... what the hell, why not.

At first I didnt like the vehicles, apparently it's set sometime in the future, but they looked more like the past to me. I wasnt all that impressed untill I blew something up and loved the graphics of the new explosions. The flame thrower looks awsome, the machine gun fires more smoothly, and the elctr gun and other added goodies are a real treat.

Just like the original GTA, i find this game so much more fun when activating cheats for infinite lives and weapons ect... if you kill people or jijack cars near cops, or kill enough people, the cops come after you. If you kill enough cops, the swat team join in, if you take out swat, the special agents come along, take out the agents, then the streets run red with military everywhere coming at you with guns, phasers & tanks. I liked that new feature... it was always fun to use a tank in the first GTA but there was only one per mission, they could only fire on a kill frenzy and once they where gone, they where gone... where as in this game, there is one hidden tank per level, but if you get the military after you, there is tanks galore... it's just too bad the other tanks will blow you to smitherines when your in one, so get out just before it blows. The invincibility/god mode cheat works well, but only on foot, if youre ina vehicle...KABOOM!

Everything else is pretty much the same as the original game, do missions, blow things up, run from this and that, take out him and her, steal one of those and take it to whatever.

I may not like the vehicles they used for this game, but the good thing about the PC version is you can do something about that. You can find various info on the net for sites where you can download new vehicles, or make your own and put them into the game... now i'm cruising around in Knightrider and the General Lee avoiding Lambourghini Cop Cars and it makes the game a lot more enjoyable.

Unless the free version is different, the only thing i did miss from the orginal was the end of level movies... i know they wernt much, but it was at least something for your reward of completing a level. Which reminds me, there is only 3 levels in this game, but unlike the first GTA, you only do the 3 levels once. But there are a whole heap of bonus games to play with this one. Just a heap of bonus stages of kill frenzies galore.

There are alot of improvements in this, and so, i still preffer the original GTA over this one, but it's not to say this game isnt as good, the only way i'd say this game was crap would be if they go back and make the original GTA game with the graphics of this game, with weaopens and bonuses and everything included.

It would be nice to see an ultimate GTA game where both this game, the original and London where all packed into the one game. And i dont mean a ppackage where you can buy all 3 together, or it has 3 discs of each game... i mean add them all into the one game, 6 or more missions, start with the original 3, then the londons, then this games and include even more to each game with it.

Anyway, this game certinly has brought out my interest to check out the latest GTA games like GTA 3 and San Andreas ect... And as soon as i buy them sometime this week, you can check out my review of them sometime soon.

review_title: Inexpensive, but not a good value as the performance is simply not there.
review_text:
The product page description for the miadore Retro N64 Controller doesn't have much confidence in its own creation, more or less pushing these as additional, secondary controllers rather than replacements for originals or more premium options. Despite the fact that it's a two-pack and really ups its value proposition if you want to create a fun multiplayer original Nintendo 64 (N64) console gameplay environment without breaking the bank, there are some serious issues with the controller.

You can definitely pay more for more premium options - even wireless solutions - but most of us these days don't play with multiple people on a local multiplayer console on a regular enough basis to justify the extra investment. And while these controllers don't mimic the unique original Nintendo controller design, they do a good job of at least superficially mimicking the modern trend of going with a more traditional layout, with the analog stick on the upper left instead of the d-pad, and in turn the d-pad in the center rather than the analog stick. This design concept does away with the triple handles of the original and is definitely easier to pick up for modern hands used to today's controller designs. Again, while this layout is not perfect for every N64 game, it can arguably work better for many of the games in the library.

My two pack was a translucent green and opaque yellow, which matched how they looked on the product page. The feel of the green plastic seemed a bit slippier than the yellow. I also noted the yellow's d-pad was more recessed than the green's, and a slightly different feel from the triggers. I don't know if it's up to manufacturing variances or simple quality control, but the green felt like a better overall performer. Unfortunately, even at this competitive price point for the pair, I was really expecting more consistency, especially since these are sold as a pair.

The analog stick feels fine and is responsive. The face buttons similarly performed well. The two sets of triggers were too recessed for my liking, resulting in mishits. The thin controller cables, which are approximately 6 feet in length, are done well and remained tangle-free.

Despite mirroring more modern designs and having a memory card/rumble pack slot, these controllers are difficult to recommend because they just don't perform like an original or slightly more expensive modern replacement controller. The poor d-pads and trigger pairs are simply unacceptable.

Bottom line, there are better options out there, so even if you're looking for an inexpensive controller addition for occasional local multiplayer battles on your original console - and you don't want to upset your friends and family - you're likely better off looking elsewhere. Fortunately, there are plenty of alternatives out there.

The hidden objects are a bit too easy to find (though I did have a few that drove me to ask for a hint). The between-game logic puzzles are familiar - Hanoi Towers, Sudoku, Mahjong solitaire - and can be skipped if you find them too difficult. The storyline is well-crafted, though it moves a bit too fast across the screen. It's not a particularly long game, unfortunately - I think it took me a total of five hours.

review_title: Good, but not quite what I was hoping for.
review_text:
The X-Men have been getting robbed of a truly excellent X-men title over the course of the last few years with the last truly great game to feature Marvel's Merry Mutants was Marvel Vs Capcom 2on the Dreamcast, (Recently ported to PS2 and Xbox.) Even in the Playstation/N64/Dreamcast era the X-men were not used outside of fighter games at all. This is the first non-fighter X-men game for a major console for a very long time, and it looked very good, and was very well advertised as well.
I rarely get so X-cited about a game that I preorder it, but I did preorder this one. Mark Hammel (Luke Skywalker) doing the voice of Wolverine... I had to see this! And he was good! Very good! The voice-overs of this game are fantastic, as is the storyline. However this is the best part of the game, and the rest really needs work, and bad.
While this game is light years better than X-men: Next Dimension it still lacks a great deal of polish that a delay of a month or so could have addressed. My biggest complaint being clipping. Clipping is when people and objects fall through walls, and things like that. To me, it's irritating, and an eye sore. The other major complaint I have is the unresponsive buttons, but that may be the fault of the Xbox controller itself. It seems that I have to hit buttons much harder on games that do not implement pressure sensitivity into the game play mechanics to get the characters to do anything. The animation could have also been better; it's pretty choppy, even though the frame rate seems fairly steady for the most part. The cut scenes are very hard for me to watch because the animation is so bad at times.
On the plus side, the camera is almost 100% controlled by the player, and that makes it easy to position just where I want it. The music is very event oriented and works well, and if you don't like it there's custom tracks.
The game is still very fun though; it's just that I wish that Activision had taken more time to polish this title up. Improving the enemy AI, improving the stealth functionality, and button responsiveness, and eliminating the clipping would have helped this game immensely. It has five stars potential, but in my opinion wasn't quite ready for shipment when it shipped. Hopefully there will be a sequel where they will address the issues that this installment has.
As with most of the cross platform games the Xbox version is the best, with GameCube second best (Frame rate issues), and Playstation 2 (Aliasing or jagged edges on top of the clipping problem) looking the worst, but despite its poor animation the character models for this game are actually pretty good, so the differences between the three versions are minimal.

review_title: An excellent keyboard for this price point
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:6730a42bdfa4554278c5877015c3e857]] Gone are the days where a keyboard with this form factor and features cost over $100.

For less than $70 this keyboard has hot swap, 3 bluetooth connections, wireless/wired connections, pudding cap keys, windows and mac key layout compatibility, and RGB, all with a 75% layout.

This is not the fanciest keyboard, but it sounds quite nice on a mat, and feels great to type on.

I bought this to try out hot swap, and was very satisfied with the results. As one can see from the video, removing the switches is relatively easy. Placing a new switch in is not hard, but care needs to be made to line the pins up fine.

The RGB on the keyboard looks great with the pudding cap keys. Having the option of updating the base RGB separately from the key RGB is a nice touch.

I've tested this on both Bluetooth and wired with no issues in connectivity.

The main drawbacks are creature comforts: the base is not adjustable (no feet), there is no physical off button (it times out after inactivity, I believe), and charging the computer takes a little while (although you can use it while charging without changing the connection method, so you can plug it in while staying connected on bluetooth).

All of these drawbacks are easy to overlook for what this package has to offer. For those looking for a 75% layout that works for both mac and PC, look no further. This is an excellent keyboard to pick up and mod, or use as is.

I recommend this product.

I didn't need the game that bad after all. Then I looked a little further down and BAM. Staring me dead in the face was the most beautiful sight ever: my beloved game at a much cheaper price. A much more reasonable price, at that! After several victory dances, much squealing, and me jibbering like an idiot to my husband, I clicked on it and ten saw it would take entirely too long to reach me. There is always a catch! But the price was too good to pass up, I had to have this game. I paid for it and anxiously awaited the email informing me that my highly coveted game was shipped, and I wasn't disappointed when it came within the hour. One you find a massive sized fish, you have to use a lot of patience and skill to get the fish on the boat because the big ones put up a heck of a fight. Sometimes you can fight with a big fish for 15+ minutes, only for the fish to get away. But like in real fishing, you won't catch all of them.

review_title: Difficult but fun game with randomly generated dungeons
review_text:
Note: I posted an update at the end. I wrote my original review after a few hours of gameplay. The update reflects 18 hours of game time.

This is a really fun game. I've been hooked on it the last two or three days. You start with one hero and you venture off into the castle. The layout is randomized each time you play. You fight enemies, leap over spikes, the usual platform game challenges. I don't really like platform games, but this has become an exception. I'm not very skilled with these types of games and my character dies A LOT. But every time you run through the game, you collect money, runes, and equipment to build yourself up. You also gain levels which appears to boost hp/mp.

When you lose, you start again, purchasing your upgrades, then venturing into a new castle totally unlike the one you last explored. There's an option to lock them down (for a 40% cut in gold intake), but it means that when you go back in any treasure chests you opened are already used, so you have to explore deeper to find new treasure. Each time you start again, you choose a new hero, which can range from spell casters to strong melee to heavy armor/high hp, to low hp spelunkers that reveal chests on the map. It's a nice variety. Also, some of the characters have status effects like "colorblind" where the levels are black and white, which can add challenge by making it more difficult to separate some enemies from the backgrounds. There is also near-sightedness which creates a blur on the screen outside a certain range of vision. There's even one that makes you play the game upside-down. I tried that one once and avoid it at all costs now.

I think the main draw of this game is that you can load this up with the intention of killing 20-30 minutes and it's still fun 2 hours later. It can be frustrating though. With randomized layouts, some rounds are going to be significantly more difficult than others. Fairy Chest rooms are the worst, sometimes having rules that just don't make sense like "no jumping" when the entire room is a series of platforms over spikes. Even if you run through the spikes, you still need to jump out of them at the end. Maybe there are runes to overcome this that I will find later.

As you upgrade your character, the gold cost of upgrades naturally increases. I'd imagine at some point this cost will become excessive, as I am already struggling to bring in enough gold for some upgrades as it is. The worst part is that you have to use your gold or lose it before reentering the castle. You have to give up any remaining gold you have to enter, so if the cheapest upgrade you have access to is 650 gold and you have 640, goodbye all 640 gold. You can reduce this toll but it costs a lot to upgrade and it appears the max is probably going to be a 30% reduction. I've only done 1/5 reductions. They don't really seem worth it, so I've been investing in more useful upgrades.

The music is good, the layouts are interesting, the game is challenging. There isn't much in terms of story. You uncover short journals as you progress. It's fine that the game is lacking in story, however. It's not the point of the game. It keeps you going with the action non-stop (except for selecting your upgrades).

Lastly, boss battles seem disproportionately difficult for the rest of the game. I'm level 60 or so now and it's getting pretty easy to clear the castle (even for someone who is terrible at these types of games), but the bosses are much much stronger than anything else you encounter.

Update: After playing for 18 hours, I've pretty much burned out on this game. All I do at this point is run dungeons over and over and over collecting money to spend on upgrades, so that hopefully I'll one day beat bosses outside the first area (the castle). The costs on everything keep going up, so it's an incredibly slow grind to unlock the incredibly large amount of upgrades. On top of that, after 18 hours I'm only level 150. I've read that the level cap is just over 500. Assuming that exp to level up increases per level, it would take 60+ hours to reach level 500. That is way too much of a time investment into grinding. I never minded putting large amounts of hours into games like Final Fantasy 7, for example, because at least you're progressing through a story at the same time. Rogue Legacy has no story.

Do I still recommend this game? Sure. I did enjoy it for 18 hours. That's a nice turnaround on a $5 game (on sale). If you're looking for a game you'll finish, however, this one probably isn't it.

I was hopeful that this case would be good. Unfortunately it's not. The right side will not close on my switch. Kind of defeats the purpose of a protective case.

While it looks gorgeous and feel ridiculously nice in my hands because it's TPU, here's why I find myself regretting not installing a custom shell instead of this, since I was mostly interested in this for the looks aspect:

A bit too thick: this can be a good thing if your switch is damage prone, but it also means the +/- buttons are harder to press due to now being caved/lower level than the case itself, and the rumble feature isn't as noticeable which people fail to mention; all the extra weight means the shock/rumble isn't going to be as strong, because that extra, encased weight absorbs it, e.g. I can only feel a mere buzz when the joycons are encased in these, and even LESS in handheld mode because again the switch is encased too! The case could certainly be thinner all around, why is it so heavy duty?

Seems like it would be fairly difficult to get off. This is also annoying as I wanted to eventually install a new kickstand and it doesn't always just pop out, you need to open your switch.

The colored buttons are next to impossible to install, because the circular sticky pads for whatever reason aren't sticky on both sides, and if they are, good luck peeling both sides successfully as they're so small. This was infuriating, because if I *could* actually install them, or install them easily, it would make the main buttons a bit easier to press due to the added depth, since again the thick case means concave buttons. Also, I'm highly doubting the sticky pads being adhesive enough for frequent, competitive play. No way in heck, not with the pads I received, at least.

In summary, outside of aesthetic and protection, this case is utterly pointless and could make certain games harder to play if anything. (Don't get me wrong, it's just so 'clean' looking, and it certainly has its place.) NOT worth more than $8-9 dollars imo, and I'm a big spender on everything you can think of, the price just seems too high to justify the value it adds, and you might have to cut the product off with heavy duty scissors to remove it because the fit is TIGHT. review_title: Doesn't work well with console FPS
review_text:
First, let me just say that I have only tried this product with FPS games on my PS3 so far. I haven't tried it with real time strategy games like Command and Conquer, so my review is based strictly off of my experience with FPS games.

I am one of the many former PC gamers out there who just cannot get used to playing FPS games with a console controller, so I decided to try my luck with this product. I was absolutely disappointed. I tried this product with Resistance, Resistance 2, Modern Warfare, and World at World, and I could not get the mouse to work correctly with any of these games. The problem here is what people call a "deadzone" and it's really my own fault for not researching this more before dropping $100 on this product. You cannot and will not be able to get the mouse to aim correctly. Believe me when I tell you that it will be nothing like playing on a PC at all. Even after all the adjusting with the mouse sensitivity and after all the different mice I've tried (Microsoft, Logitech, even old school ball mouses), I cannot get it to work correctly. Your aim will be all over the place. In fact, using this thing actually made me a bit better at using the console controller because I got so fed up with it that I went back to using a regular controller.

Also, they should have added a third USB port to this thing. Right now, if you want to configure the keyboard, you need to unplug the mouse and vice versa. Small annoyance, but it's something they should've thought of, especially if they are charging $100 for this thing.

The only reason I didn't give this product a 1-star rating was because the keyboard part of this thing actually works very well. I was able to map all my FPS buttons to the keyboard without any issues. Plus it worked perfectly in the game. Unfortunately, it doesn't make a difference if you can't aim your gun at anything. Bottom line, I would stay away from this product if you plan on using it for FPS games on the PS3.

review_title: One of the best NES games ever
review_text:
Take the best parts of Legend of Zelda, Metroid, a vertical space shoot-em up, very smooth and fast responses to the controls, make a single game out of it, and then fail to advertise it at all.

That is "The Guardian Legend". This game has excellent music, a variety of bosses, a map that actually tells you where you need to go for the next major boss (ignoring dozens of minor bosses on the Zelda-like walk-around map), and also serves as your special weapon selection screen.

As an RPG, your score also doubles as experience, meaning your shield strength goes up at certain scores. You use energy chips to power special weapons, and as a side effect the more chips you have, the more powerful (and faster) your main gun shoots.

Look up this game on Youtube to get an idea of what it is like, and you will realize what a disservice Broderbund did to this game. As far as I can tell, there was no advertising done for it anywhere. Once you've played through the start of this game, you will understand why this is a shame.

The only nitpick is that the password to continue your game is 32 characters long, composed of upper case, lower case, numbers, and symbols. Fortunately, it includes a password check screen, where you can test the password you just wrote down to make sure it is correct, without that affecting your game in progress. Other than that, you will get hours of enjoyment out of this game.

If nothing else, hold down A+B, then reset the NES. You will get to the music test screen, and can enjoy that for BGM for another game (and there is a lot of music to choose from).
